features.description: Copies a tab, including its back/forward history, into a new tab next to it.
features.notes: Copy the entries with webContents.navigationHistory.getAllEntries() and load them with navigationHistory.restore() (Electron 32+).

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the most recently closed tab, window or tab group in its old position, with its history.
features.notes: Keep a closed-items stack holding nav entries, index, group, window and position. Restore with navigationHistory.restore.

features.description: Group tabs under a colored, named label. Groups can be collapsed or expanded, renamed, recolored, ungrouped, closed, or moved to a new window, and you can drag tabs in and out.
features.notes: Custom tab-strip model. Animate collapse and expand. Chrome uses 9 group colors.

features.description: Save a tab group so it shows in the bookmarks bar / Tab groups menu, reopen it later, and sync it across devices.
features.notes: Local saving is easy. Syncing across devices needs our own sync backend (Lumio server).

features.description: Share a tab group with other people so everyone can see and edit the same set of tabs.
features.notes: Needs our own collaboration backend (invite links, realtime updates). Not possible through Google.

features.description: A dropdown (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A) that fuzzy-searches open tabs across all windows plus recently closed tabs, and can close or switch to them.
features.notes: Custom popover. Use fuzzy matching on title and URL.

features.description: Hovering a tab shows a card with the full title, domain, an optional live preview image, and memory usage or 'inactive tab' status.
features.notes: Thumbnail from webContents.capturePage(). Memory from app.getAppMetrics() matched through webContents.getOSProcessId().

features.description: With many tabs open, they shrink down to just a favicon. Newer Chrome can also scroll the tab strip, with scroll buttons.
features.notes: Custom layout algorithm. Smooth horizontal scroll and fade masks at the edges.

features.description: Show two tabs side by side in one window with a draggable divider. You can swap sides, close one side, or turn the split back into separate tabs.
features.notes: Two WebContentsViews with setBounds driven by a divider. Needs a focus indicator for the active pane.

features.description: Shift-click or Cmd/Ctrl-click to select several tabs, then move, close, group, pin, bookmark or drag them together.
features.notes: Custom tab-strip selection model.

features.description: Right-click a tab for: New tab to the right, Add to group, Move to another window, Reload, Duplicate, Pin, Mute site, Close, Close other tabs, Close tabs to the right, Add to reading list, Bookmark, Split view.
features.notes: Native Menu.popup or a custom-styled menu.

features.description: Loading spinner, favicon, crashed-tab icon, network-error state, a dot when a background tab changes its title (notifications), and a discarded/inactive marker.
features.notes: Driven by the did-start-loading/did-stop-loading, page-favicon-updated, page-title-updated and render-process-gone events.

features.description: Icons on a tab show when it is recording, using the camera or microphone, sharing the screen, or connected to Bluetooth/USB/HID/serial devices.
features.notes: There is no direct 'in use' API. Track it from the permission handler grants, setDisplayMediaRequestHandler and device-select events, and infer when use ends with a preload that watches MediaStreamTrack 'ended'.

features.description: Show tabs as a vertical list in a sidebar instead of across the top. Chrome is rolling this out in 2025-26.
features.notes: A second rendering of the same tab model. A good differentiator, and it pairs well with groups.

features.description: Drop a link, file or text onto the strip to open it in a new tab, or onto a tab to load it in that tab. An arrow marks where it will land.
features.notes: HTML5 drag-and-drop in the browser-chrome renderer. Text becomes a search.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+N and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N. Incognito windows have a dark theme and their own icon.
features.notes: A BaseWindow per window. Incognito uses a non-persistent session partition.

features.description: Give a window a custom name that shows in Mission Control, the taskbar and the Window menu.
features.notes: BaseWindow.setTitle plus a stored name.

features.description: macOS traffic lights inside the tab strip and the green-button fullscreen/tiling. Windows caption buttons with Snap Layouts on hover over maximize. Window size, position and maximized state are restored.
features.notes: titleBarStyle 'hiddenInset' on Mac. titleBarOverlay or Window Controls Overlay on Windows keeps Snap Layouts working. Persist window bounds.

features.description: One box for URLs and searches. As you type it completes URLs inline, and it decides whether input is a URL or a search query.
features.notes: Custom autocomplete engine. Use URL heuristics: a valid TLD (public suffix list), localhost, IP addresses, schemes.

features.description: Live query suggestions from the default search engine as you type.
features.notes: Google's suggest endpoint (suggestqueries.google.com, client=chrome/firefox) works without a key but is unofficial. Bing, DuckDuckGo and Brave have suggest endpoints too. Debounce requests, and skip them in incognito if suggestions are turned off.

features.description: Ranks previously visited pages, bookmarks and typed shortcuts by how often and how recently you used them, and learns from what you pick.
features.notes: Local history DB (SQLite / IndexedDB) with a frecency score and FTS on titles.

features.description: If the URL you're typing is already open, the suggestion offers a 'Switch to this tab' button.
features.notes: Match against the open tabs in the tab model.

features.description: Choose the default engine (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, Ecosia and others) and add, edit or remove engines with %s URL templates.
features.notes: Settings UI plus a stored list.

features.description: Type a keyword such as 'yt' then Tab to search that site from the omnibox. Engines are detected automatically from OpenSearch tags and listed as inactive shortcuts.
features.notes: Detect the <link rel=search> OpenSearch description with a preload script or a fetch.

features.description: @tabs, @bookmarks, @history and @gemini limit suggestions to that source.
features.notes: Same autocomplete providers, filtered. @gemini can map to Lumio's AI chat.

features.description: Typing '12*8' or '5 km in miles' shows the answer directly in the dropdown.
features.notes: Local math or unit library (e.g. math.js). Currency conversion needs a rates API.

features.description: Instant answers such as weather, definitions, sports scores, stock prices and translations inside the suggestions.
features.notes: Chrome gets these from Google's private suggest response. We'd need separate APIs (weather, dictionary) or our own AI server.

features.description: Suggestions with thumbnails (people, places), plus trending or recent searches when the box is focused and empty.
features.notes: Recent searches and most-visited sites are local and easy. Entity images and trending need search-provider data.

features.feature: Paste and go / paste and search
features.description: Right-clicking the omnibox offers to paste and immediately navigate or search.
features.notes: Custom context menu on the omnibox input.

features.description: Shift+Delete, or the X on a history suggestion, removes it from history and suggestions.
features.notes: Delete from the local history DB.

features.description: Ctrl+Enter adds www. and .com, Alt/Opt+Enter opens in a new tab, Shift+Enter opens in a new window, Esc reverts, and arrow keys move through suggestions.
features.notes: Key handling in the omnibox component.

features.description: Hides https:// and www. until the box is focused, emphasizes the domain, and has an 'Always show full URLs' toggle. Clicking selects everything, and copying gives the full URL. You can drag the URL or the site-info chip out.
features.notes: Custom formatting. The copied value must always be the full canonical URL.

features.description: Icons inside the omnibox for bookmark (star), zoom level, translate, saved password key, install app, blocked pop-ups or permissions, cookies, share, Lens and reading mode.
features.notes: Custom icon slots with appear/disappear animations.

features.description: Typing commands like 'clear browsing data', 'manage passwords' or 'update browser' offers a button that does it.
features.notes: A static action list matched by keywords.

features.description: Punycode display for confusable domains, plus 'Did you mean <real site>?' warnings for lookalike URLs.
features.notes: Chromium's IDN spoof checker is not exposed to Electron. Re-implement with url.domainToASCII, a confusables table and a top-sites list.

features.description: On first run, ask the user to pick a default search engine. Chrome is required to do this in the EU.
features.notes: Part of the first-run flow.

features.description: A mic button for speaking a search on the omnibox or New Tab Page.
features.notes: Chrome's webkitSpeechRecognition uses Google servers and doesn't work in Electron. Use Lumio's own speech-to-text (voice is already built).

features.description: Adds https:// automatically (falling back to http), handles single-word intranet hosts ('Did you mean http://wiki/?'), and handles localhost:port.
features.notes: Heuristics in the navigate function.

features.description: Back and forward buttons. Long-press or right-click either one to see a list of earlier pages and jump to any of them.
features.notes: webContents.navigationHistory (canGoBack, goToIndex, getAllEntries).

features.description: Reload, hard reload that ignores the cache (Shift-click or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R), and Stop (Esc). The reload button turns into a stop button while the page loads.
features.notes: reload(), reloadIgnoringCache(), stop(). 'Empty cache and hard reload' with DevTools open uses session.clearCache().

features.description: An optional toolbar button that goes to the New Tab Page or a custom home page.
features.notes: Toggle in Appearance settings.

features.description: A find bar (Cmd/Ctrl+F) with a match count, next and previous (Cmd+G / Shift+Cmd+G), highlighted matches, and a marker for the active match.
features.notes: webContents.findInPage / stopFindInPage plus the 'found-in-page' event for counts. Animate the bar sliding in.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl +, -, 0 and Ctrl+scroll. Zoom is remembered per site, a zoom bubble with a Reset button appears, and the omnibox shows a zoom icon when the level isn't 100%.
features.notes: setZoomLevel/getZoomLevel. Electron zooms per origin by default. Persist the levels for the Site settings > Zoom levels list.

features.description: Trackpad pinch zoom and double-tap smart zoom on Mac.
features.notes: Electron disables this by default. Turn it on with webContents.setVisualZoomLevelLimits(1, 3).

features.description: Two-finger horizontal swipe on a trackpad goes back or forward, with an animated arrow overlay.
features.notes: Chrome's overscroll navigation isn't in Electron. The 'swipe' event only fires for three-finger swipes. Build it from wheel events with phases ('input-event' or a preload) plus a custom arrow animation.

features.description: A print preview pane with destination, pages, layout, color, margins, scale, headers and footers, background graphics, and Save as PDF.
features.notes: Electron has webContents.print() (system dialog) and printToPDF(), but not Chrome's print preview UI. Build a custom preview from printToPDF output and send it to a printer with print({deviceName}). The macOS system dialog already includes a preview.

features.description: Save as Webpage Complete, HTML Only, or a single MHTML file.
features.notes: webContents.savePage(path, 'HTMLComplete' | 'HTMLOnly' | 'MHTML').

features.description: view-source:URL (Cmd+Opt+U / Ctrl+U) shows the raw HTML with line numbers and line wrapping.
features.notes: Electron doesn't reliably support the view-source: scheme. Re-fetch the page with the session (net.fetch with the same cookies) and render it in a lumio:// page with syntax highlighting.

features.description: Distraction-free text view in the side panel with font, size, line and letter spacing, color themes, and read aloud with word highlighting.
features.notes: Mozilla Readability run in the page through executeJavaScript. Read aloud through speechSynthesis or Lumio TTS (Chrome's natural voices are Google's).

features.description: F7 puts a movable text cursor in pages so you can select text with the keyboard.
features.notes: Chromium's caret-browsing pref isn't exposed in Electron. Could be approximated by injecting a script, or by testing whether the Chromium switch can be enabled.

features.description: Browser full screen (Ctrl+Cmd+F / F11) and HTML5 element full screen (videos) with a 'Press Esc to exit' bubble. On Mac, the toolbar shows when you hover at the top.
features.notes: setFullScreen plus the enter-html-full-screen / leave-html-full-screen events. Hide the browser chrome and show the exit bubble.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+O opens local files. file:// directory listings let you browse folders.
features.notes: Opening files works. Chromium's directory-listing template may be missing in Electron, so we may need a custom lumio:// directory view.

features.description: View PDFs in a tab with a thumbnails sidebar, zoom, fit, rotate, page navigation, search, download, print, form filling and ink annotations.
features.notes: Electron includes Chromium's PDF viewer (plugins enabled). The basics work. Annotation and saving edits may be limited, so test and fall back to pdf.js if needed.

features.description: Opening an image, video, audio or plain-text URL shows it in a built-in viewer. Images get click-to-zoom.
features.notes: Handled by Chromium's core rendering.

features.description: Hovering a link shows its URL in a bubble at the bottom-left, which expands after a delay.
features.notes: webContents 'update-target-url' event plus a custom overlay with fade animation.

features.description: Animated smooth scrolling, and middle-click autoscroll on Windows.
features.notes: Smooth scrolling is Chromium default. Middle-click autoscroll may need a Chromium feature flag or a custom implementation.

features.feature: Text fragments & Copy link to highlight
features.description: Links with #:~:text= scroll to and highlight that text. Right-click a selection and choose 'Copy link to highlight' to create such a link.
features.notes: Scrolling to text is built into Chromium. Generate the fragment ourselves in JS (Chrome's generator isn't exposed).

features.feature: Network error pages & offline dino game
features.description: Friendly pages for DNS errors, no internet, timeouts and refused connections, each with an error code, Reload, and the dinosaur game when offline.
features.notes: 'did-fail-load' (ignore -3 ERR_ABORTED), then load a custom error page. Our own offline mini-game would be a branding opportunity.

features.description: When a renderer crashes or runs out of memory, the tab shows an error page with a Reload button.
features.notes: 'render-process-gone' event with its reason (crashed, oom, killed).

features.description: 'Page unresponsive' prompt offering Wait or Exit page.
features.notes: 'unresponsive' and 'responsive' events. Exit with forcefullyCrashRenderer().

features.description: alert, confirm and prompt shown as dialogs attached to the tab, showing the page's origin, with 'Prevent this page from creating additional dialogs'.
features.notes: Electron shows alert and confirm as native app-modal dialogs. window.prompt() is NOT supported in Electron, so add a preload polyfill with sync IPC and a custom tab-modal UI.

features.description: Asks for confirmation before leaving a page with unsaved changes.
features.notes: 'will-prevent-unload' event. Show our own dialog and call event.preventDefault() to leave anyway.

features.description: Username and password prompt for sites using Basic or Digest auth and for proxy auth.
features.notes: 'login' event with a custom dialog that passes the callback(user, pass).

features.description: 'Open Zoom.us?' style prompt before handing zoommtg:, mailto:, slack: and similar links to other apps, with an 'Always allow' option.
features.notes: Intercept in will-navigate / setWindowOpenHandler, then shell.openExternal after the user confirms. Store the allowed origin+scheme pairs.

features.description: Blocks pop-ups the user didn't trigger. An omnibox icon lists the blocked pop-ups, with 'Always allow from this site'.
features.notes: Chrome's pop-up blocker lives in the Chrome layer and isn't in Electron. setWindowOpenHandler doesn't say whether the user triggered the pop-up, so track user activation in a preload (navigator.userActivation) and decide from that.

features.description: Pop a video out into a floating always-on-top window, from the right-click menu, the site's own button, or the media hub.
features.notes: requestPictureInPicture works in Electron. Trigger it on a page's video with executeJavaScript.

features.description: Document Picture-in-Picture (for example a Meet call in PiP) and automatic PiP when you switch away from a tab playing video.
features.notes: The Document PiP API is in Chromium core, so test it. Automatic PiP on tab switch is a Chrome-layer feature, so call requestPictureInPicture ourselves when the tab is hidden.

features.description: A toolbar media hub listing every tab playing audio or video, with artwork, title, play/pause, skip, seek, PiP and 'go to tab'.
features.notes: No Electron API for this. Track the media-started-playing / media-paused events, read navigator.mediaSession metadata through a preload, and send actions through executeJavaScript.

features.description: Keyboard play/pause/next keys control the active media. Media shows in macOS Now Playing and Windows SMTC.
features.notes: Chromium's HardwareMediaKeyHandling works in Electron and uses mediaSession metadata.

features.description: Cast a tab, the desktop or a video to Chromecast or Google TV devices.
features.notes: Media Router and Cast are not in Electron, and the Presentation API is unsupported. Leave it out, or offer a third-party castv2 library just for media URLs.

features.description: Play protected content on Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, Prime Video and Hulu.
features.notes: Stock Electron does NOT include Widevine. Use castlabs Electron for Content Security (ECS) with VMP signing (EVS) for release builds. Without VMP, many services refuse to play or drop to low resolution. This is a launch blocker for many users.

features.description: H.264, AAC, MP3 and HEVC (through the system decoder) playback.
features.notes: Electron's ffmpeg build includes the proprietary codecs.

features.description: Chrome blocks autoplay with sound based on how much you engage with a site. Site settings > Sound allows or mutes a site.
features.notes: Set a global autoplay policy with app.commandLine 'autoplay-policy'. Handle per-site sound with setAudioMuted. Chrome's engagement-based scoring is not available.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+D or the star in the omnibox opens a bubble to set the name and folder, remove the bookmark, or open the editor.
features.notes: Local bookmarks store, synced through our own server.

features.description: A toolbar under the omnibox with bookmarks and folder dropdowns. It can be always shown, shown only on the New Tab Page, or hidden (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B). It has an overflow chevron, drag to reorder, drag-in to add, and middle-click 'Open all'.
features.notes: Custom UI. Folder menus can be native Menus or custom popovers.

features.description: A full page (Cmd+Opt+B / Ctrl+Shift+O) with a folder tree, search, sort A-Z, multi-select, cut/copy/paste, drag and drop, edit, delete with undo, and Open all in new window or incognito.
features.notes: Built as an internal lumio://bookmarks page.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D saves every open tab into a new folder.
features.notes: Iterate over the tab model.

features.description: Import bookmarks, history, passwords, search engines and autofill from Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox, Brave, or an HTML file.
features.notes: Chrome's 'Bookmarks' JSON and 'History' SQLite are readable. Chrome passwords need a Keychain/DPAPI decrypt prompt ('Chrome Safe Storage'). Safari needs Full Disk Access. Firefox uses places.sqlite. The HTML (Netscape) format is easy.

features.description: Export all bookmarks to the standard HTML bookmarks file.
features.notes: Generate the Netscape bookmark HTML.

features.description: Save pages to read later, with read/unread sections, an unread count, and it's available offline in the side panel.
features.notes: Local store plus sync. Optionally cache with savePage MHTML for offline reading.

features.description: 'All bookmarks' in the side panel with compact or visual views, sorting, editing, and drag to tabs.
features.notes: Shares the bookmarks store.

features.description: Default folders for bookmarks that aren't on the bar and for bookmarks synced from a phone.
features.notes: 'Other' is trivial. 'Mobile' needs our sync plus the companion app.

features.description: Track a product's price and get notified when it drops (Chrome Shopping).
features.notes: Uses Google Shopping data in Chrome. Would need our own scraping or an AI backend.

features.description: History grouped by day with time, favicon and title. Search, delete individual items or selections, 'More from this site', and open in a new tab.
features.notes: Our own history DB fed from did-navigate events, with FTS search.

features.description: Groups related visits and searches into topics ('Journeys'), with related searches.
features.notes: Chrome uses on-device clustering. Ours would use heuristics or Lumio's AI embeddings.

features.description: The History menu shows recently closed tabs and windows plus tabs from other devices.
features.notes: Recently closed is local. Other devices need our sync.

features.description: A dialog (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Delete) with a time range (last 15 min, hour, 24 h, 7 days, 4 weeks, all time). Data types: history, cookies & site data, cached images & files, download history, passwords, autofill, site settings, hosted app data. Shows counts of what will be removed.
features.notes: History and downloads are our own DB, so time ranges are easy. Electron's session.clearData / clearStorageData / clearCache don't support time ranges for cookies, storage or cache. Cookies can be filtered by creation time. Cache and storage would be all-time only.

features.description: One click deletes the last 15 minutes of browsing.
features.notes: Same limits as above for storage. History is fine.

features.description: Restores tabs, groups, pinned state, windows and back/forward history at startup. After a crash it shows a 'Restore pages?' bubble.
features.notes: Periodically write the session file (tabs plus nav entries) and restore with navigationHistory.restore. Detect an unclean exit with a flag file.

features.description: Search your history in natural language ('that recipe site with the blue header last week').
features.notes: Store page text or embeddings locally and answer with Lumio's AI. Watch privacy, and offer an opt-in.

features.description: A toolbar icon with an animated progress ring, plus a bubble listing recent downloads with open, show in folder, pause and cancel.
features.notes: session 'will-download' event plus DownloadItem 'updated' / 'done' events. A strong place for polished animation.

features.description: A downloads page (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J) with a full list, search, open, show in folder, remove from list, clear all, and retry.
features.notes: Our own download history DB.

features.description: Pause and resume, and resume interrupted downloads after a network drop or restart.
features.notes: DownloadItem.pause/resume/canResume. Use session.createInterruptedDownload to resume after a restart.

features.feature: Download location & ask where to save
features.description: A default download folder, plus an optional 'Ask where to save each file' prompt.
features.notes: DownloadItem.setSavePath or setSaveDialogOptions inside will-download.

features.feature: Auto-open file types / open when done
features.description: 'Always open files of this type' and 'Open when done'.
features.notes: shell.openPath when the download finishes. Never auto-open executables.

features.description: Warnings for malicious, uncommon or dangerous file types, insecure (HTTP) downloads and encrypted archives, with Keep or Delete options.
features.notes: Safe Browsing download protection needs Google. We can warn on risky extensions (.exe, .dmg, .pkg, .scr…), on HTTP downloads from HTTPS pages, and against hash blocklists. Chromium still sets the macOS quarantine attribute so Gatekeeper checks the file.

features.description: Drag a finished download from the bubble or page into Finder, Explorer or another app.
features.notes: webContents.startDrag({file, icon}).

features.description: Download progress on the Dock or taskbar icon, a count badge, and a Dock bounce when it finishes.
features.notes: BrowserWindow.setProgressBar, app.dock.setBadge, app.dock.downloadFinished.

features.description: Asks before a site downloads several files automatically.
features.notes: Count downloads per page without a user gesture in will-download, then prompt.

features.description: Separate profiles, each with its own bookmarks, history, cookies, extensions, theme, name and avatar, opening in separate windows.
features.notes: session.fromPartition('persist:profile-<id>') per profile, plus a separate data folder for bookmarks and settings.

features.description: A toolbar avatar menu to switch, add or manage profiles, plus an optional profile picker at startup.
features.notes: Custom UI.

features.description: A temporary profile with no saved data, wiped when the window closes.
features.notes: An in-memory (non-persist) partition.

features.description: Private windows that save no history, cookies or form data. Third-party cookies are blocked by default, extensions are off unless allowed, it has a dark theme and a tab counter, and you can close all incognito windows at once.
features.notes: A non-persistent partition shared by all incognito windows of a profile. Skip history, downloads-list and omnibox learning.

features.description: Sign into the browser with an account to turn on sync. An avatar shows in the toolbar.
features.notes: Chrome/Google account sign-in isn't possible. Use the Lumio account (Google OAuth through the system browser or a loopback redirect).

features.description: A desktop or Dock shortcut that opens a specific profile directly.
features.notes: Windows .lnk with a --profile argument is easy. On Mac it would need separate app wrappers.

features.description: Enterprise-managed profiles with policies, and Family Link supervised accounts.
features.notes: Family Link is Google-only. Enterprise policy support would mean our own JSON policy file. Low priority.

features.description: Sync bookmarks, history, open tabs, passwords, settings, extensions, themes, reading list, tab groups and addresses across devices, with per-type toggles.
features.notes: Must be our own server (the Lumio Worker). Use end-to-end encryption, at least for passwords. Google sync is not usable.

features.description: Encrypt synced data with a passphrase the server can't read.
features.notes: Client-side crypto (WebCrypto / libsodium) before upload.

features.description: Send the current page to another signed-in device, where it shows as a notification.
features.notes: Through our sync server plus the phone companion app's push notifications.

features.description: See and open tabs that are open on your other devices.
features.notes: Needs our sync, uploading open-tab lists.

features.description: On macOS, continue the current page on an iPhone or another Mac.
features.notes: app.setUserActivity('NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb', {webpageURL}) works on Mac with entitlements.

features.description: After a login or signup form is submitted, a bubble offers to save or update the password (Never for this site is also an option).
features.notes: Chromium's password manager is not in Electron. Detect forms in a preload (form submit, fetch, or navigation after typing) and store encrypted with safeStorage. This is significant engineering.

features.description: A key icon and a dropdown under username/password fields fill saved credentials, including in iframes.
features.notes: A custom overlay positioned from field bounds in the preload. Fill strictly by exact origin to avoid leaks, and require a user gesture.

features.description: Suggests a strong password on signup and new-password fields and saves it automatically.
features.notes: crypto.getRandomValues, plus autocomplete='new-password' detection.

features.description: A page to search, view, edit, delete and add notes to saved passwords. Revealing or copying needs Touch ID, Windows Hello or the system password.
features.notes: systemPreferences.promptTouchID on Mac. Windows Hello needs a native module, or fall back to the OS password via a credential prompt.

features.description: Flags compromised (in a data breach), reused and weak passwords and links to change them.
features.notes: Use the HIBP Pwned Passwords k-anonymity range API (free, no key), plus local checks for reuse and weakness.

features.description: Import passwords from a CSV file and export them to one.
features.notes: Use the Chrome CSV format (name,url,username,password,note). Require OS auth before exporting.

features.description: Create and use passkeys and hardware security keys, using iCloud Keychain or Windows Hello as the platform authenticator, or a phone over a QR code (hybrid).
features.notes: Electron's WebAuthn support is limited. Security keys and Windows Hello generally work on Windows. macOS Touch ID / iCloud Keychain passkeys need Apple entitlements and aren't wired up in Electron. Hybrid (phone QR) isn't supported. Test with Google, GitHub and Apple logins.

features.description: Save, edit and fill name, address, phone and email in forms.
features.notes: Chromium autofill isn't exposed. Build field classification from autocomplete attributes and name/label heuristics in a preload.

features.description: Save cards, fill checkout forms, ask for the CVC or device auth, and offer virtual cards / Google Pay.
features.notes: Card storage and fill can be custom (encrypted, OS-auth gated). Google Pay and virtual cards are not possible. Consider skipping card storage at launch for liability reasons.

features.description: Suggests values you've typed into similar fields before.
features.notes: A custom preload that records non-sensitive fields. Never record passwords or card numbers.

features.description: Uses AI to fill complex forms from saved info (Chrome 2025).
features.notes: Possible with Lumio's AI and the user's saved profile data. Needs opt-in.

features.description: A lock/tune icon in the omnibox opens a panel showing whether the connection is secure, the certificate, cookies and site data, permission toggles, and links to site settings. HTTP pages show 'Not secure'.
features.notes: Custom bubble. Get the security state from the scheme, certificate-error events and the CDP Security domain.

features.description: Shows certificate details (subject, issuer, validity, fingerprints) and the certificate chain.
features.notes: There's no built-in viewer. Capture certificates with session.setCertificateVerifyProc or the certificate-error event and render our own viewer. dialog.showCertificateTrustDialog exists on Mac and Windows.

features.description: A full-page 'Your connection is not private' warning with the error code, Advanced, and Proceed (unsafe).
features.notes: Handle 'certificate-error' with a custom interstitial. Remember the proceed decision per host for the session.

features.description: Choose a client certificate when a site requests one.
features.notes: 'select-client-certificate' event plus a chooser UI.

features.description: Opens the OS certificate store.
features.notes: shell.openPath on Keychain Access (Mac) or certmgr.msc (Windows).

features.description: Red warning pages for phishing, malware and unwanted software. Has Standard and Enhanced protection, and warns about leaked passwords and dangerous downloads.
features.notes: Needs a Google Safe Browsing API key, which is for non-commercial use only, or the paid Web Risk API for commercial use. Alternatively use open blocklists (URLhaus, OpenPhish, PhishTank) with our own interstitial. Enhanced protection is not possible.

features.description: Upgrades navigations to HTTPS and warns before loading an HTTP-only site.
features.notes: Rewrite to https in will-navigate or webRequest. On failure, show our own 'Continue to site' interstitial and remember the exception.

features.description: Use secure DNS with the current provider or a custom one (Cloudflare, Google, NextDNS, etc.).
features.notes: app.configureHostResolver({secureDnsMode, secureDnsServers}).

features.description: Allow third-party cookies, block them in incognito, or block them everywhere, with per-site exceptions and the 'eye' icon to allow them temporarily for a site.
features.notes: Electron has no CookieSettings switch. We can strip Cookie / Set-Cookie on third-party requests through webRequest, but document.cookie and storage in iframes need more work (preload overrides or a Chromium flag). Test carefully.

features.description: 'Clear cookies and site data when you close all windows', with exceptions.
features.notes: session.clearStorageData on quit, filtered by origin exceptions.

features.feature: Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control
features.description: Send DNT (and GPC) signals with requests.
features.notes: Add headers in webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders, and navigator.globalPrivacyControl in a preload.

features.description: Chrome only blocks intrusive ads on sites that violate the Better Ads standards. A built-in tracker/ad blocker would go further and set us apart.
features.notes: @ghostery/adblocker-electron with EasyList and EasyPrivacy, with per-site toggles.

features.description: Ad topics, site-suggested ads and ad measurement controls.
features.notes: These are Google ad features. Not applicable, so turn the APIs off.

features.description: Each site runs in a sandboxed renderer process, isolated from other sites.
features.notes: Keep sandbox:true, contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false and minimal preload IPC for web content. This is critical for a browser built on Electron.

features.description: One-click check of update status, compromised passwords, extensions, Safe Browsing, unused site permissions and notification spam.
features.notes: Combine our own checks. Some items depend on the features above.

features.description: A step-by-step walkthrough of privacy settings (cookies, history sync, Safe Browsing, search suggestions).
features.notes: A custom settings page.

features.description: Blocks or auto-upgrades HTTP subresources on HTTPS pages.
features.notes: Chromium core behavior.

features.description: Keeps WebRTC from leaking local or public IPs (mostly a policy or extension setting).
features.notes: webContents.setWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy.

features.description: IP protection and fingerprinting protection in incognito (Chrome 2025+).
features.notes: IP protection needs a proxy network. Basic fingerprinting protection is possible through a preload.

features.description: Prompts for location, camera, microphone, notifications, MIDI, clipboard and more, with Allow, Allow this time and Don't allow, shown as an animated omnibox chip or bubble.
features.notes: session.setPermissionRequestHandler plus a custom chip or bubble UI.

features.description: 'All sites' with storage use and a reset button, per-permission lists of allowed and blocked sites, and per-site detail pages.
features.notes: Persist decisions and enforce them in setPermissionCheckHandler and setPermissionRequestHandler.

features.description: Web notifications shown as OS notifications, quieter prompts for spammy sites, and permission review.
features.notes: Electron routes the web Notification API to native notifications.

features.description: Gives sites your location after you allow it.
features.notes: macOS uses Core Location (needs an Info.plist usage string). Windows and Linux may fall back to Google's network location service, which needs GOOGLE_API_KEY.

features.description: Choose the default camera and microphone in settings and switch per site from the page info bubble.
features.notes: getUserMedia works. A preferred-device setting needs a preload that adjusts the constraints.

features.description: Pick a tab, window or entire screen to share, with system/tab audio, and a 'Sharing this tab' bar with Stop.
features.notes: session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler with desktopCapturer.getSources. Can share another tab by passing its WebFrameMain. Option: {useSystemPicker:true} on macOS 15+.

features.feature: USB / HID / Serial / Bluetooth device chooser
features.description: Lets sites connect to hardware after you pick a device from a chooser.
features.notes: The select-usb-device, select-hid-device, select-serial-port (session) and select-bluetooth-device (webContents) events plus a chooser UI.

features.description: Lets sites read and save local files and folders after you allow it.
features.notes: Chromium core plus the permission handler for 'fileSystem'.

features.description: JavaScript, images, pop-ups & redirects, intrusive ads, automatic downloads, sound, insecure content, and V8 optimizer, each on or off per site.
features.notes: JavaScript and images are webPreferences fixed when the view is created, so recreate the view or inject a CSP to change them per site. Pop-ups, sound and downloads are handled in our own handlers.

features.description: Sites like Gmail register to open mailto: and similar links (navigator.registerProtocolHandler).
features.notes: Not supported in Electron. Polyfill registerProtocolHandler with a preload plus our own routing.

features.description: Automatically removes permissions from sites you haven't visited in a while and tells you.
features.notes: Timestamp each grant and expire it.

features.description: The browser's 'Sign in with…' account chooser for the FedCM API.
features.notes: The FedCM UI is in the Chrome layer and absent in Electron. Sites fall back to pop-up OAuth, which works.

features.description: See and delete cookies and storage per site, and see storage used.
features.notes: session.cookies.get/remove per domain. Storage usage via the CDP Storage.getUsageAndQuota through webContents.debugger. Clear with clearStorageData({origin}).

features.description: Choose whether PDFs download or open in the viewer.
features.notes: Branch on the response mime type in will-download or the navigation handler.

features.description: Browse the Chrome Web Store and click 'Add to Chrome' to install extensions and themes.
features.notes: The electron-chrome-web-store package enables installing CRX files from the Web Store and updating them. Check Google's Web Store terms. API coverage limits which extensions actually work.

features.description: Popular extensions rely on the tabs, windows, action, contextMenus, storage, scripting, webRequest, declarativeNetRequest, sidePanel, offscreen, identity, commands and notifications APIs.
features.notes: Electron implements only a subset. electron-chrome-extensions adds tabs, windows, action, contextMenus, commands, cookies and notifications. Missing or weak: declarativeNetRequest (so uBlock Origin Lite breaks), identity, sidePanel, native messaging. Test the top 20 extensions.

features.description: A puzzle-piece menu listing extensions with pin/unpin to the toolbar, site access per extension, and 'Manage extensions'.
features.notes: Custom UI. Render action icons with electron-chrome-extensions <browser-action-list>.

features.description: Clicking an extension icon opens its popup. Icons show badge text and color.
features.notes: Supported through electron-chrome-extensions. Popup sizing and focus need polish.

features.description: Enable or disable, Details (permissions, site access, allow in incognito, allow file URLs), Remove, Errors.
features.notes: session.extensions.getAllExtensions / removeExtension plus our own state.

features.description: Load unpacked, Pack extension, Update, inspect service worker or background page.
features.notes: session.extensions.loadExtension(path). Inspect via DevTools on the extension's target.

features.description: A page to assign keyboard shortcuts to extension commands.
features.notes: The commands API is partially available through electron-chrome-extensions.

features.description: Extensions update in the background.
features.notes: electron-chrome-web-store supports updates. Unpacked extensions don't update.

features.description: Extensions talk to desktop apps (1Password, Bitwarden, Grammarly desktop integration).
features.notes: Not supported in Electron. Password-manager extensions lose desktop-app unlock but may still work in standalone mode.

features.description: Warns about malware, policy-violating or MV2 (unsupported) extensions.
features.notes: Check the manifest version. Malware flags would need our own blocklist.

features.description: Frees memory from inactive tabs (Moderate, Balanced and Maximum modes) and reloads them when you return. Has an 'Always keep these sites active' list and shows memory saved.
features.notes: Electron doesn't expose Chromium tab discarding. Destroy the background WebContentsView, keep its nav entries, and restore on activation. Exclude tabs playing audio, using forms or capturing.

features.description: On battery or low battery, limits background activity, frame rate and visual effects.
features.notes: powerMonitor on-battery events. setBackgroundThrottling(true). Freeze background tabs with CDP Page.setWebLifecycleState('frozen'). Turn off browser-UI animations. setFrameRate only applies to offscreen rendering.

features.description: Hover cards show that a tab is inactive and how much memory it saved.
features.notes: Comes from our discard model.

features.description: Notifies you when tabs use a lot of CPU or memory and offers to deactivate them.
features.notes: Poll app.getAppMetrics().

features.description: Shift+Esc opens a per-tab, extension, GPU and utility process list with memory, CPU, network and process ID, plus End process.
features.notes: app.getAppMetrics() matched to webContents.getOSProcessId(). Count network through webRequest. End process with forcefullyCrashRenderer().

features.description: Standard or extended preloading: preconnect, DNS prefetch, and prerendering omnibox and New Tab Page suggestions.
features.notes: session.preconnect. Speculation-rules prerendering is partly in the content layer. Omnibox prerendering would need a hidden WebContentsView that we swap in.

features.description: Back and forward return instantly by restoring the page from memory.
features.notes: A Chromium feature that may be off by default in Electron. Test it, and enable it with --enable-features=BackForwardCache if stable.

features.description: Device, Light or Dark mode for the browser UI. Web pages get the matching prefers-color-scheme.
features.notes: nativeTheme.themeSource ('system' | 'light' | 'dark') affects both the UI and pages. Every UI surface (tabs, omnibox, menus, bubbles, settings, NTP, PDF) needs light and dark design tokens. This is the user's 'white mode' requirement.

features.description: A live panel to choose theme colors, background image and NTP options, and to customize the toolbar.
features.notes: Custom side panel with instant preview animations.

features.description: A palette of preset colors plus a custom color picker that builds tonal UI colors (Material You style). Can follow the background image or wallpaper.
features.notes: Generate tonal palettes (e.g. @material/material-color-utilities) for light and dark.

features.description: Install theme packs (images and colors) from the Chrome Web Store.
features.notes: Parse the CRX manifest 'theme' key (images, colors, tints) and map it onto our tokens.

features.description: Pin or unpin toolbar buttons: home, forward, reading mode, translate, print, Lens, cast, task manager, copy link, Gemini, tab search position.
features.notes: A config-driven toolbar with drag to arrange.

features.description: Show home button, show bookmarks bar, show tab groups in bookmarks bar, show full URLs, show images on tab hover cards, show memory usage on hover cards.
features.notes: Settings flags.

features.description: Choose whether the side panel opens on the left or the right.
features.notes: Layout flag.

features.description: Font size presets, standard, serif, sans-serif and fixed-width fonts, and minimum font size.
features.notes: webPreferences defaultFontFamily, defaultFontSize and minimumFontSize are fixed when a view is created. Changes apply to new tabs, or recreate existing ones.

features.description: A global default zoom level for all sites.
features.notes: Apply setZoomLevel when a site has no per-site override.

features.description: Automatically darkens web pages (a Chrome flag).
features.notes: Chromium has a ForceDark web-content setting that may work through a switch. Otherwise inject a Dark Reader style.

features.description: Smooth tab, bubble, omnibox dropdown, side panel and download animations. Chrome uses subtle, quick Material motion.
features.notes: The user wants the best animations. Use spring/FLIP animations, keep them at 60-120 fps on the compositor (transform/opacity only), and respect prefers-reduced-motion and Energy Saver.

features.description: Compact and touch-friendly sizing for the tab strip and toolbar.
features.notes: CSS variables.

features.description: A resizable panel beside the page with a selector for which panel to show, pinning to the toolbar, and opening and closing animations.
features.notes: Shrink the page WebContentsView bounds and animate them. Each panel can be an internal page or a separate WebContentsView.

features.description: Browse and search history without leaving the page (Chrome 2025).
features.notes: Reuses the history DB.

features.description: Google search results or Lens results open in the side panel next to the page.
features.notes: We can load any search results URL in a side-panel WebContentsView. Lens-specific integration is Google's.

features.description: Extensions add their own side panel (chrome.sidePanel API).
features.notes: The sidePanel API isn't in Electron. We'd have to shim it.

features.description: Take notes tied to pages in the side panel (Chrome experiment, power bookmarks).
features.notes: A simple local store plus sync. Optional differentiator.

features.description: Open the New Tab Page, continue where you left off, or open a specific set of pages (with 'Use current pages').
features.notes: Settings plus session restore.

features.description: A search box (routes to the omnibox) and up to 10 shortcut tiles, most-visited or custom, which you can add, edit, remove or hide, with undo.
features.notes: Internal lumio://newtab page with favicons from our cache.

features.description: Upload an image, pick from collections, refresh daily, or use a solid color. Credits are shown.
features.notes: Our own image collections (Unsplash API with our own key, or bundled images).

features.description: Cards to resume recent tabs or journeys, shopping carts, and so on.
features.notes: 'Recently visited' and 'continue reading' are easy. Shopping and other cards need data.

features.description: Doodles and Google-account New Tab Page features.
features.notes: Google-only. Show our own branding.

features.description: Make the home button open the New Tab Page or a custom URL.
features.notes: Setting.

features.description: Extensions can replace the New Tab Page.
features.notes: Read chrome_url_overrides.newtab from installed extensions.

features.description: Welcome pages: sign in, import from another browser, set as default, pick a theme and search engine.
features.notes: Custom onboarding flow. A good place for polished animations.

features.description: VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS and Narrator work with page content and with the browser UI.
features.notes: Chromium's accessibility tree works in Electron. The custom browser UI must use semantic HTML and ARIA (roles for tablist and tab, menus, live regions).

features.description: F6 cycles between toolbar, page, bookmarks and panels. Alt+Shift+T focuses the toolbar. Arrow keys move around the tab strip and menus, with visible focus rings.
features.notes: Custom focus management across views (webContents.focus()).

features.description: Automatic captions for any audio or video playing in the browser, optionally translated.
features.notes: Chrome uses the on-device Google SODA model, which isn't in Electron. Capture tab audio and run our own speech-to-text (Whisper or Lumio's server). Heavy, so likely post-launch.

features.description: Shows a quick highlight ring around the focused element.
features.notes: A preload-injected CSS and JS overlay.

features.description: Generates alt text for unlabeled images for screen readers (Chrome uses a Google service).
features.notes: Possible with our own vision model. Needs opt-in.

features.description: Reduced motion, high or increased contrast, reduced transparency, and larger text.
features.notes: nativeTheme.shouldUseHighContrastColors and prefersReducedTransparency, the CSS media queries prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-contrast, and systemPreferences.getAnimationSettings on Windows.

features.description: Text-to-speech of the page from reading mode, with speed and voice choice.
features.notes: speechSynthesis (system voices) or Lumio TTS. Chrome's natural voices are Google's.

features.description: Back, Forward, Reload, Save as, Print, Cast, Search with Lens, Translate, Open in reading mode, View page source, Inspect.
features.notes: webContents 'context-menu' event with params, shown with Menu.popup or a custom menu.

features.description: Open in new tab, new window, incognito window, split view or another profile. Save link as, Copy link address, Copy link text, Create QR code.
features.notes: params.linkURL / linkText. Save link via webContents.downloadURL.

features.description: Open image in new tab, Save image as, Copy image, Copy image address, Search image with Lens, Create QR code for image.
features.notes: webContents.copyImageAt(x, y) and downloadURL(srcURL). Lens is partially feasible (see Sharing & capture).

features.description: Copy, Search <engine> for '…', Copy link to highlight, Translate selection, Print, Speech.
features.notes: params.selectionText. Translate needs an API.

features.description: Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Paste as plain text, Select all, spelling suggestions, Add to dictionary, Emoji & Symbols, Writing direction, password generation and autofill entries, Help me write.
features.notes: params.isEditable, misspelledWord, dictionarySuggestions; webContents.replaceMisspelling, pasteAndMatchStyle; app.showEmojiPanel.

features.description: Loop, Show controls, Picture in picture, Save video as, Copy video address, Open video in new tab.
features.notes: params.mediaType, srcURL and mediaFlags. Apply actions with executeJavaScript on the element at the click point.

features.description: Items that extensions add through the contextMenus API.
features.notes: electron-chrome-extensions provides contextMenus integration.

features.description: View frame source, Reload frame.
features.notes: params.frame / frameURL.

features.description: Copy link, Send to your devices, Create QR code, Cast, Save page as, and on macOS the native Share sheet (AirDrop, Messages, Mail).
features.notes: Electron ShareMenu on Mac. Send to devices and Cast have their own limits.

features.description: Creates a QR code for the page, link or image URL, with a center logo and Copy/Download.
features.notes: qrcode npm library. Use our logo in place of Chrome's dino.

features.description: Capture the visible area, a selected region or the full page, then copy, download or annotate.
features.notes: webContents.capturePage(rect). Full page via CDP Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}).

features.description: Select any region of the page (Lens overlay) or an image to search visually, translate text, or ask questions.
features.notes: No official Lens API. Public image URLs can open lens.google.com/uploadbyurl. Captured regions need an unofficial upload. Alternative: Lumio's AI vision on a region screenshot ('Ask about this').

features.feature: Install site as app / Create shortcut
features.description: Install PWAs into their own windows with a Dock or Start menu icon, or create a desktop shortcut.
features.notes: Electron has no PWA install or app shim support. We could open an app-style window from the web manifest, but OS-level app shortcuts need custom launchers.

features.description: An AI assistant with page context (summarize, ask about the tab, compare multiple tabs), in a floating window or the side panel.
features.notes: Use Lumio's own AI (model picker already exists) with page text from executeJavaScript. Gemini itself isn't available.

features.description: Right-click a text field to draft or rewrite text with AI.
features.notes: Own LLM plus the editable context menu.

features.description: AI suggests tab groups with names.
features.notes: Send titles and URLs to our LLM and get groups back.

features.description: Summarize the current page or ask questions about it.
features.notes: Own LLM with Readability-extracted text.

features.description: An AI agent that clicks, types and navigates to finish tasks (Chrome agent mode, 2025-26).
features.notes: Lumio already has tools and workflows. Needs strong confirmation UI for sensitive actions.

features.description: An AI-generated comparison table of products across open tabs.
features.notes: Own LLM plus page extraction.

features.feature: Scam / tech-support detection with on-device AI
features.description: Chrome uses Gemini Nano to warn about scam pages.
features.notes: On-device Gemini Nano isn't available. Server-side analysis raises privacy concerns.

features.description: Elements, Console, Sources, Network, Performance, Memory, Application, Security, Recorder. Dock bottom, right, left or undocked.
features.notes: webContents.openDevTools({mode}). Could host it in a custom WebContentsView through setDevToolsWebContents.

features.description: Right-click > Inspect jumps to the element in DevTools. Cmd+Shift+C opens the element picker.
features.notes: webContents.inspectElement(x, y).

features.description: Responsive device toolbar, network and CPU throttling, sensors.
features.notes: Built into DevTools. Works when DevTools is open.

features.description: Performance, SEO and accessibility audits from DevTools.
features.notes: The Lighthouse panel may be missing from Electron's DevTools build. Run Lighthouse through CDP as a fallback.

features.description: chrome://inspect, --remote-debugging-port, Android device inspection.
features.notes: --remote-debugging-port works. A chrome://inspect UI and Android device inspection are not included.

features.description: chrome://settings, history, downloads, extensions, flags, version, gpu, media-internals, webrtc-internals, net-export.
features.notes: Some content-layer pages (chrome://gpu, accessibility, media-internals, webrtc-internals) exist in Electron. Settings, history and similar pages must be our own lumio:// pages. flags becomes a 'Labs' page applying command-line switches at restart.

features.description: Offers to translate foreign-language pages. Options: always translate a language, never translate a language or site, choose the target language, show original.
features.notes: Chrome's built-in translate (Google service or on-device) isn't available. Needs an API (Google Cloud Translate with our own key, DeepL, or Lumio's LLM), injected to translate DOM text nodes. Costs money per character.

features.description: Translate highlighted text from the context menu, inline.
features.notes: Same API requirement.

features.description: Detects the language a page is in, which triggers the translate offer.
features.notes: Use <html lang> plus a JS detector (franc or cld3-asm) on sampled text.

features.description: An ordered list of languages for websites (Accept-Language).
features.notes: session.setUserAgent(ua, acceptLanguages).

features.description: Show the browser interface in a chosen language.
features.notes: Our own i18n (at least EN and ES) plus the Chromium --lang switch at launch.

features.description: Basic spell check with red squiggles, suggestions, language selection, and a custom dictionary you can add to and manage.
features.notes: Electron spellchecker: Hunspell on Windows and Linux, the native checker on macOS. Uses session.setSpellCheckerLanguages and addWordToSpellCheckerDictionary. Dictionaries download from Google's CDN by default; host them ourselves with setSpellCheckerDictionaryDownloadURL.

features.description: Google's cloud spell and grammar check.
features.notes: Google-only service. Could use LanguageTool or an LLM instead.

features.description: A settings button and a first-run prompt to make the app the default browser, with an 'is default' status.
features.notes: app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient('http'/'https') plus Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes and HTML CFBundleDocumentTypes on Mac (macOS shows its own confirmation). Windows needs registry Capabilities, then opens Settings > Default apps for the user to confirm.

features.feature: Open links and files from other apps
features.description: Clicking links in other apps, or opening .html and .pdf files, opens them in the browser.
features.notes: app 'open-url' / 'open-file' events (Mac), 'second-instance' argv (Windows), requestSingleInstanceLock.

features.description: 'Use graphics acceleration when available', applied after a relaunch.
features.notes: Call app.disableHardwareAcceleration() before ready, based on a stored preference.

features.description: Use the system proxy or a custom/PAC proxy.
features.notes: session.setProxy / app.setProxy, or open the OS proxy settings as Chrome does.

features.description: 'Continue running background apps when the browser is closed'.
features.notes: Keep the app alive after windows close. Needs a tray or menu bar icon on Windows.

features.description: 'Warn before quitting' (hold Cmd+Q on Mac) and a confirmation when closing a window with many tabs.
features.notes: before-quit and close handlers plus a hold-to-quit overlay.

features.description: File, Edit, View, History, Bookmarks, Profiles, Tab, Window and Help menus with all their items and shortcuts.
features.notes: Menu.setApplicationMenu with dynamic History and Bookmarks submenus.

features.description: Dock menu (New Window, New Incognito Window), Windows jump list, taskbar thumbnails, badges.
features.notes: app.dock.setMenu, app.setJumpList, setThumbarButtons.

features.description: Sends crash reports so problems can be fixed.
features.notes: crashReporter.start pointed at our own endpoint or Sentry, opt-in.

features.description: Restore settings to their original defaults (keeps bookmarks, history and passwords).
features.notes: Settings-store reset.

features.description: Emoji picker, macOS Services menu, dictation, and Look Up (force-click a word for its definition).
features.notes: app.showEmojiPanel. The macOS text services mostly work in Electron, but Look Up / force-click need testing.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+T new tab, +N new window, +Shift+N incognito, +W close tab, +Shift+W close window, +Shift+T reopen, Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab next/prev tab, Cmd+Opt+Right/Left next/prev tab (Mac), Cmd/Ctrl+1-8 jump to tab, Cmd/Ctrl+9 last tab, Cmd+M minimize, Cmd+Q / Ctrl+Shift+Q quit, Cmd+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+A tab search.
features.notes: Menu accelerators plus before-input-event so shortcuts still work when the page has focus. Let pages capture keys where Chrome does.

features.description: Cmd+L / Ctrl+L / Alt+D / F6 focus omnibox, Cmd+Opt+F / Ctrl+K / Ctrl+E search, Ctrl+Enter add www/.com, Alt/Opt+Enter open in new tab, Shift+Enter open in new window, Shift+Delete remove suggestion, Esc revert.
features.notes: Omnibox key handling.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+F find, +G / Shift+G next/prev match, Cmd+R / F5 reload, Cmd+Shift+R / Ctrl+F5 hard reload, Esc stop, Cmd+[ / ] or Alt+Left/Right back/forward, Backspace (off by default), Cmd/Ctrl+P print, +S save, +D bookmark, +Shift+D bookmark all, +Plus/Minus/0 zoom, Space/Shift+Space scroll, Home/End, Ctrl+Cmd+F / F11 fullscreen, F7 caret browsing.
features.notes: Accelerators plus before-input-event.

features.description: Cmd+Shift+B / Ctrl+Shift+B bookmarks bar, Cmd+Opt+B / Ctrl+Shift+O bookmark manager, Cmd+Y / Ctrl+H history, Cmd+Shift+J / Ctrl+J downloads, Shift+Esc task manager, Cmd+Opt+I / F12 DevTools, Cmd+Opt+J / Ctrl+Shift+J console, Cmd+Opt+U / Ctrl+U view source, Cmd+Shift+Delete / Ctrl+Shift+Del clear data, Cmd+, settings, Cmd+Shift+M / Ctrl+Shift+M switch profile, Alt+Shift+I feedback, Alt+Shift+T toolbar focus, F6 cycle panes, Alt+F / Alt+E app menu.
features.notes: Accelerators. Also publish a shortcuts reference page.

features.description: Cmd/Ctrl-click: open link in background tab. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift-click: foreground tab. Shift-click: new window. Middle-click: new tab or close tab. Opt/Alt-click: download link. Drag link to tab strip. Ctrl+scroll: zoom. Shift+scroll: horizontal scroll. Mouse back/forward buttons.
features.notes: setWindowOpenHandler gives disposition (foreground-tab, background-tab, new-window). Mouse buttons 4 and 5 arrive via app-command (Windows) or a preload.

features.description: Change browser shortcuts and assign shortcuts to extensions.
features.notes: Our own keymap settings.

features.description: New tab, window and incognito window; profile row; Passwords and autofill; History; Downloads; Bookmarks and lists; Tab groups; Extensions; Delete browsing data; Zoom row; Print; Search with Google Lens; Translate; Find and edit; Cast, save and share; More tools; Help; Settings; Exit.
features.notes: A custom animated menu or a native Menu with matching submenus.

features.description: Save page as, Create shortcut / Install, Name window, Delete browsing data, Performance, Task manager, Developer tools, Reading mode.
features.notes: Maps to the features above.

features.description: Zoom -, %, + and a fullscreen button right inside the menu, plus a Cut/Copy/Paste row.
features.notes: Easy in a custom HTML menu, harder in a native Menu.

features.description: When an update is ready, the menu button turns into a colored 'Update' chip (green, orange, red by age) and 'Relaunch to update' appears in the menu.
features.notes: Driven by autoUpdater 'update-downloaded'. Restore the session after relaunch.

features.description: Sections: You and Google (Lumio account), Autofill and passwords, Privacy and security, Performance, Appearance, Search engine, Default browser, On startup, Languages, Downloads, Accessibility, System, Reset settings, Extensions, About.
features.notes: lumio://settings with left navigation and deep links to sections.

features.description: Search box that filters sections and highlights matching settings, with a 'no results' state.
features.notes: Index setting labels and keywords, then highlight and scroll to matches.

features.description: Version, channel, 'Checking for updates' / 'Up to date' / 'Relaunch'. Updates download automatically in the background.
features.notes: electron-updater / Squirrel with signed builds (an Apple-signed release already exists). Show release notes.

features.description: A help link and a 'Report an issue' form (Alt+Shift+I) that can attach a screenshot, URL and system info.
features.notes: Custom feedback form posting to our server. Ask before including the screenshot or URL.

features.description: After an update, shows a page with the new features.
features.notes: Open lumio://whats-new once per version.

features.description: Sites (Gmail, Slack, Discord, news) send push notifications through service workers, even when the tab is closed.
features.notes: Electron has no push service (Chrome uses Google's FCM/GCM), so pushManager.subscribe fails. Notifications from open tabs still work. Worth stating as a known limitation.

features.description: Websites' voice input (webkitSpeechRecognition), such as dictation on Google Search, Docs or translator sites.
features.notes: Chrome sends audio to Google's speech servers, and that's unavailable in Electron. Sites fall back or break. Only possible with a polyfill that injects our own STT.

features.feature: Modern web APIs (WebGL, WebGPU, WASM, WebRTC, WebCodecs, WebUSB…)
features.description: Pages using modern platform features work the same as in Chrome.
features.notes: These come with the Chromium version Electron ships. Keep Electron current; it trails Chrome stable by about 0-1 versions.

ui.summary:
CURRENT LOOK: Lumio Browser is dark-only and restrained, styled to match lumio-usa.online. The window chrome is near-black (--bg #070708). UI text is Geist, display headlines are Instrument Serif, section labels are Geist Mono uppercase eyebrows, and the accent is soft blue (#86b7ff, which the profile theme color can change). Buttons are pills, cards and popovers are rounded (12-22px), and borders are thin white-alpha hairlines. The tab strip uses floating rounded tabs, the omnibox is a filled rounded field with an accent focus ring, and the page sits in a rounded 10px slot with an 8px gutter. The most finished parts are the AI panel (drawer slide in shell.css:344-368 that respects prefers-reduced-motion, plan checklist, composer, effort slider), the agent aura (aura.css, which has proper enter and exit animations and reduced-motion handling) and the welcome flow.

WHAT HOLDS IT BACK:
(a) Motion only covers entrances. Almost everything uses the `pop` or `rise` keyframes, nothing animates out, tabs do not animate when they open, close or reorder, and there is no page-load progress bar.
(b) The page area jumps around because the native WebContentsView resizes when the permission bar, bookmarks bar, find bar or downloads button appears.
(c) There are two real CSS bugs. `@keyframes breathe` is defined twice in shell.css (233 and 470), which breaks the account "connecting" pulse. The `.ring` class is used by both the downloads button and the usage ring, which breaks the downloads progress ring.
(d) Overlay dropdowns (suggestions, account menu, site info) only play their entrance animation the first time.
(e) Colors are hard-coded in four separate stylesheets: 151 hex literals in shell.css and 76 in overlay.css, `color-scheme: dark` is fixed, and native background colors are set in main/window.js and main/tabs.js. This blocks white mode until shared tokens exist.
(f) Accessibility gaps: buttons that only appear on hover stay invisible when they get keyboard focus, tabs cannot be reached with the keyboard, toggle switches show no focus, `--label` text on cards is about 4.2:1 contrast, and reduced-motion is only handled in 6 places.
(g) Pages are inconsistent: buttons come in 5 heights, there are 18 font sizes and 17 border-radius values, 3 different section-label styles, native confirm()/alert() dialogs, and empty states that are plain gray text with no loading states.

Everything proposed below can be done in plain CSS/JS on Electron 43 (recent Chromium). It uses `interpolate-size`, `@starting-style`, `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, View Transitions, container queries and `@property`, all of which this Chromium version supports.

Key files: /Users/juan/Developer/lumio-browser/renderer/ui/shell.css, shell.js, shell.html, ai-panel.js, sidebar.js, overlay.css, overlay.js; /Users/juan/Developer/lumio-browser/renderer/pages/pages.css, lists.css, newtab.css, newtab.js, settings.css, settings.js, history.css, downloads.js, passwords.js, welcome.css, error.html; /Users/juan/Developer/lumio-browser/main/window.js, main/tabs.js.

issues.where: renderer/ui/shell.css:232-233 and 466-470
issues.problem: `@keyframes breathe` is defined twice. The later one (opacity .25 + scale .7, meant for the streaming dot) wins, so `.account-btn.connecting .avatar` shrinks and fades the avatar instead of showing the intended accent ring pulse.
issues.fix: Rename the keyframes to `ring-breathe` (box-shadow ring, account button) and `dot-breathe` (streaming dot). Better still, animate the ring as an ::after element with a static shadow and an opacity pulse.

issues.where: renderer/ui/shell.css:244-252 vs 748 (.ring {width:18px;height:18px;transform:rotate(-90deg)}); shell.html:42; panel-extras.js:160
issues.problem: The downloads button's `<span class="ring">` also matches the usage-ring rule `.ring`. That rule makes the span an 18x18 box anchored at its top-left inset (3px,3px), so it is off-center and rotated -90deg. The radial mask (transparent until 10.5px) then shows only the box corners, so the progress ring renders as corner slivers.
issues.fix: Rename the downloads ring to `.dl-ring`, or scope the usage rule to `.ring-btn .ring`. Register `@property --p { syntax:'<number>'; inherits:true; initial-value:0 }` so the conic progress animates smoothly.

issues.where: renderer/pages/downloads.js:76-78 (setInterval → load) and 49-57 (innerHTML render); lists.css:22
issues.problem: Every second the page re-renders the whole list with innerHTML whenever it has focus, even when nothing is downloading. Keyboard focus, hover state and text selection are lost every second, and the progress-bar width transition never runs because the nodes are recreated.
issues.fix: Poll only while some download is progressing. Diff rows by id: update `.bar i` with style.transform scaleX(p) and `.sub` textContent in place, and only insert or remove changed rows.

issues.where: renderer/ui/shell.css:433 (scroll-behavior: smooth), 438-439 (.msg rise); ai-panel.js:454-457 scrollDown, 662-676 renderChat
issues.problem: Opening or switching a chat rebuilds every message and each one plays `rise` at the same time. `scroll-behavior: smooth` on #messages makes the `scrollTop = scrollHeight` assignment animate, so a long chat visibly scrolls through its whole history. During streaming the smooth scroll lags behind the growing content, the <140px 'near bottom' check fails, and auto-follow stops.
issues.fix: Remove scroll-behavior from #messages and keep programmatic scrolling instant. Use scrollTo({behavior:'smooth'}) only for a user-triggered 'Jump to latest' button. Animate only live messages (add `.msg.new`, or put `.instant` on #messages during renderChat).

issues.where: renderer/ui/ai-panel.js:702-707 flushText (renderMd of full buffer every rAF); shell.html:76 (#messages aria-live=polite)
issues.problem: Every animation frame re-parses the whole answer as markdown and replaces innerHTML. The cost grows with answer length, so long answers stutter near the end. Because the container is aria-live, screen readers re-announce the message over and over.
issues.fix: Split the buffer at the last finished block (a blank line outside a code fence). Keep finished blocks in the DOM and re-render only the tail block. Set aria-busy="true" on the live message while it streams, and announce completion through a visually-hidden role=status element.

issues.area: Overlay dropdowns (suggestions, account, site info, downloads, password save)
issues.where: renderer/ui/overlay.css:15-17; main/window.js:58-66 (setBounds+addChildView, then send data), 68-76 (instant remove); overlay.js:200-228
issues.problem: The #card `in` animation plays only once per window: the overlay document is never reloaded, and it is only attached and detached. The view is also attached before the new payload renders, so the previous dropdown's content can flash for a frame. Measured menus then jump in height when overlay:size arrives (rAF plus a 150ms timer). Closing is an instant removal.
issues.fix: In overlay.js, on each `overlay-data` that starts a new show, call card.getAnimations().forEach(a=>a.cancel()) and run card.animate(...). In hideOverlay, send `overlay-clear` so the card is blank before the next show. Measure before showing: render first and let the overlay report its size, and only then have main call addChildView. Add a 90ms exit: main sends `overlay-out` and removes the view after 100ms unless it is shown again.

issues.where: shell.html:56-61 + shell.js:611-622 (permbar); shell.js:405-411 (bookmarks bar NTP-only); shell.html:31-37 (findbar in toolbar flex row); shell.js:374 (downloads button hidden→shown); shell.css:188-192 (toast inside omnibox)
issues.problem: Several pieces of chrome push the page around when they appear. The permission infobar shifts the whole web page down about 44px. With the bookmarks bar off, the bar appears and disappears on every navigation to or from the new tab page, so the page moves 32px. The find bar squeezes the omnibox by about 230px. The first download inserts a 30px button that shifts the toolbar. Toasts squeeze the URL.
issues.fix: Show permission prompts as an overlay bubble anchored to #site-icon, reusing the pwsave pattern at shell.js:310-318. Animate the bookmarks-bar grid row height (grid-template-rows transition, 180ms) and let the #slot ResizeObserver follow, as the panel already does. Position the find bar absolutely over the right end of the toolbar. Fade the downloads button into reserved space, or accept the shift but animate it. Move long toasts out of the omnibox (see the toast item).

issues.area: White mode blocked by hard-coded colors
issues.where: shell.css:32 + pages.css:8 + settings.css:128 (color-scheme: dark); 151 hex literals in shell.css, 76 in overlay.css; main/window.js:59-60 (titleBarOverlay + backgroundColor '#080808'); main/tabs.js:88,165 ('#0c0c0d'/'#ffffff'); newtab.js:4 (#ededee/#86b7ff in SVG)
issues.problem: Tokens only cover part of the UI. Surfaces such as #composer (#18181b/#36363b, shell.css:575), popovers (#161619f5), the sidebar (#0a0a0b), overlay rows (#262628/#303033) and white-alpha hairlines (#ffffff0d etc.) are literals. The native window and view backgrounds are also fixed dark, so a light theme would produce dark flashes and unreadable controls.
issues.fix: Create a shared renderer/assets/tokens.css with semantic tokens for dark and light (see designSystem). Replace white-alpha literals with color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) N%, transparent). Drive nativeTheme.themeSource from a setting, and derive the window backgroundColor, titleBarOverlay and view background colors from the resolved theme.

issues.where: shell.css:138-139 (.tab .x opacity 0), 424-425 (.li-del), 460-461 (pre .copy), 770-771 (.made-img .acts), 906-907 (.sb-dots); history.css:25-26 (checkbox opacity 0), 34-35 (.acts); lists.css:30-31, 36-37; switches shell.css:726-731, lists.css:57-62, settings.css:8-13
issues.problem: Controls that only appear on hover stay at opacity 0 when they receive keyboard focus, so focus lands on invisible buttons and checkboxes. Toggle switches hide the real input (opacity 0, width 0) and have no `input:focus-visible + i` style, so their focus is invisible. Other focus rings are inconsistent: the UA default ring in most places, an accent ring on #plan-head (544), and only a background change on .menu-row and .sb-row.
issues.fix: Add a global token ring: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px }`. Add `:focus-within` next to every `:hover` reveal rule. Add `.switch input:focus-visible + i { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px }`.

issues.where: renderer/ui/shell.js:57-61 (div role=tab, no tabindex), 66 (context menu only by right-click)
issues.problem: Tabs cannot be reached with Tab or arrow keys. There is no roving tabindex, no aria-controls, and no keyboard way to open the context menu or close a tab apart from shortcuts.
issues.fix: Use a roving tabindex on .tab elements (tabindex 0 on the active tab, -1 on others), with ArrowLeft/Right, Home/End, Delete to close, and Shift+F10 / ContextMenu key to open tab:context.

issues.where: shell.css:111 (#tabs min-width 0, no overflow handling), 119 (.tab min-width 44px), 141-143; shell.js:102-104 (narrow via rAF + offsetWidth)
issues.problem: With many tabs, each tab bottoms out at 44px and the tabs then overflow the #tabs box, overlapping the + button and the drag area. The `.narrow` class is only computed when tabs change (not on window resize) and only after a frame, so the title or X flickers and stays wrong after resizing.
issues.fix: Replace the JS narrow check with CSS: `.tab { container-type: inline-size }` and `@container (max-width: 75px) { .title, .audio { display:none } }`. Give #tabs `overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none` with fade masks at both ends, scroll the active tab into view, or shrink to favicon-only first.

issues.where: renderer/ui/shell.js:141-147
issues.problem: On pointerup all transforms are cleared before main replies with the new order. The dragged tab flashes back to its old slot for a frame or two, then jumps to its new place.
issues.fix: On drop, move the element to the target index in the DOM yourself and keep a FLIP from its current visual offset to 0 (200ms --ease-out), then send tab:move. If main's next `tabs` state disagrees, FLIP back.

issues.where: settings.js:108 is the only page that sets --accent; 22 literal #86b7ff in pages (newtab.css:1 gradient, pages.css:27 .field:focus, settings.css:47,66, welcome.css:4,10,44,54, history.css:16 selbar #1b2433); shell.css 15 literals (e.g. 620-621 slider, 650-654 page-suggest, 846-854 wf-card, 917/921 inputs)
issues.problem: When the user picks purple, green or another theme color, the new tab page, history, welcome, focus borders and several shell components stay blue.
issues.fix: Expose the profile theme through INTERNAL_PRELOAD (or a page:init call) and set --accent in a shared page bootstrap. Replace blue literals with color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) N%, transparent).

issues.where: renderer/pages/settings.css:27 (@media max-width:820px → .side display:none)
