issues.where: shell.css:15-16 (--field and --hover both #18181b), 60 (.icon-btn:hover var(--hover)), 165/169 (#omnibox field / field-hover); star + pw-key in shell.html:28-29
issues.problem: The star and key buttons inside the omnibox hover to #18181b, which matches the omnibox background and is darker than the hovered omnibox (#1f1f23). Hover feedback is either invisible or looks like a hole.
issues.fix: Add `#omnibox .icon-btn:hover { background: var(--active) }`. Long term, define --hover as a translucent overlay, e.g. color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 7%, transparent), so it works on any surface.

issues.where: overlay.css:19 (.row.sel, .row:hover), shell.css:419 (.list-item:hover, .list-item.sel), 843 (.wf-menu .menu-row.sel)
issues.problem: The row under the mouse and the row selected with the keyboard are highlighted at the same time with the same style, so after pressing an arrow key two suggestions look selected.
issues.fix: Make mousemove set the selection, so there is a single highlight. For example, a `.sel-pill` element moved with transform (see the omnibox animation).

issues.where: Only shell.css:366,402,570,623, newtab.css:42, aura.css:53 handle it. Unguarded: shell.js:381 + ai-panel.js:786 (WAAPI), shell.css:305-311 slot glow, 821-826 agent-pulse, 472-478 shimmer, 438/485/502 rise, 193 pop; newtab.css:2 (.nt not in the line-42 rule); welcome.css:11, 43-44 (infinite pulse); error.html:9; history.css:16; settings.css:86
issues.problem: Many entrance animations and several infinite loops (the agent glow for a whole agent run, pulses, shimmer) ignore prefers-reduced-motion.
issues.fix: Add a global safety net in tokens.css: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){*,*::before,*::after{animation-duration:.01ms!important;animation-iteration-count:1!important;transition-duration:.01ms!important;scroll-behavior:auto!important}}`, exempting `.spinner` (a slow 1.6s spin). Add renderer/ui/motion.js exporting `reduced` and `anim(el,kf,opts)` that shortens WAAPI calls.

issues.where: shell.css:305-311 (#slot box-shadow glow, 2.4s infinite), 233 (breathe box-shadow), 821-826 (agent-pulse box-shadow on every helper tab), 790/804-805 (mic/orb shadows)
issues.problem: Animating box-shadow repaints every frame. The slot glow runs for the whole duration of an agent task, alongside native page rendering.
issues.fix: Draw the glow once on a pseudo-element (#slot::after with a static box-shadow) and animate only its opacity (and transform for pulses), adding will-change: opacity while the agent is running.

issues.where: shell.css:15 --label #76767e (pages.css:5 same); overlay.css:22,30 #7c7c80 on #161619
issues.problem: Secondary text at 11-12.5px measures about 4.2:1 on --card #111114 and about 4.4:1 on the overlay card, which is below WCAG AA (4.5:1). It is used for timestamps, hints, URLs and sublabels everywhere.
issues.fix: Raise --label to about #8a8a93 (about 5.5:1 on #111114) and route overlay grays through the same token.

issues.where: shell.css:3-33 vs pages.css:3-9 (--card2, --line2, --sans; no --hover/--active/--fast) vs overlay.css:4 (only --accent; grays #8a8a8a #7c7c80 #9a9a9a #a3a3aa #cfcfcf #bbb #eee) vs aura.css (none); --chrome defined but unused
issues.problem: The four surfaces (shell, overlay, internal pages, aura) define their own palettes, so the same role gets different values and names.
issues.fix: Create a single renderer/assets/tokens.css, imported by shell.css, overlay.css, aura.css and pages.css the same way fonts.css is today, and delete the local :root blocks.

issues.where: 18 font sizes 9-17px in half steps across ui/pages CSS; 17 radii in shell.css; buttons: shell .btn 28px (65-73), pages .btn 34px (pages.css:17), .btn.small 28px (lists.css:9) vs 30px (welcome.css:69), overlay .acc-btn 30px pill vs .dl/.si-actions buttons radius 7px (overlay.css:33,56), doc-btn 26, wf-run 30, vb-end 30; inputs 30/32/34/38px with radii 8/9/10/12
issues.problem: Controls with the same role look different from one surface to the next, and the same class name is defined twice with different values.
issues.fix: Use one button component (sm 28 / md 32 / lg 44, pill), one field (32 / 38, --r-lg), one icon-button (26 / 30, --r-md), and a type scale of 11/12/13/14/16 plus serif display sizes (see designSystem).

issues.where: Mono .12em: shell.css:414 .list-label, pages.css:31 h2, newtab.css:49 h3, settings.css:26. Geist 600 uppercase .6px: history.css:20 .day, lists.css:7. Geist 600 uppercase .5px: overlay.css:35 .head, 51 .si-sec, 144 .ss-label
issues.problem: Eyebrow and section labels change typeface, tracking and size from one surface to the next.
issues.fix: Use a single `.eyebrow` class (Geist Mono 500, 11px, .12em, uppercase, var(--text-3)) everywhere.

issues.where: settings.js:528,533,646,649,724,745,750,752; passwords.js:149,192 (confirm/alert); history.html:34-57 + history.css:50-51 (<dialog> without enter or exit animation)
issues.problem: OS-styled confirm() and alert() boxes break the visual language and block the page. The one custom dialog appears instantly.
issues.fix: Add a shared page module dialog.js with confirmDialog({title, body, confirmLabel, danger}) returning a Promise. It renders an animated <dialog> (see the dialog animation) and focuses the safe action by default.

issues.where: lists.css:8 + history.css:40 (plain gray text); lists.css:65-66 (extensions has a hero empty state); downloads.js:60-63, history.js, passwords.js, sidebar.js:107-118 (nothing shown while awaiting data); history.js:79 ('Loading more…' text); newtab.html:13 + newtab.js:51-52 ('Lumio' swaps to the greeting after the await); newtab.js:125 (sites appear late)
issues.problem: Empty states differ by page, and no page shows anything while its data is loading, so content pops in and moves the layout. The new tab heading visibly changes text during its entrance animation.
issues.fix: Use one empty-state component: a 48px rounded icon tile (like error.html .ico), a title, one line of text and an optional CTA. Show skeleton rows (3-6 bars with a subtle shimmer, reduced-motion safe) in the initial HTML and crossfade to data (150ms). Compute the time-of-day greeting synchronously and fade in only the name.

issues.where: shell.css:188-193; shell.js:354-361 (fixed 2200ms, hidden instantly); main/main.js:398,537 (~100-char messages)
issues.problem: Long messages are forced onto one line (nowrap) inside the omnibox. They crush the URL, get clipped, and disappear after 2.2s before anyone can read them. There is no exit animation and no role=status.
issues.fix: Keep short confirmations (Bookmarked, Page saved) in the omnibox. Show long ones as an overlay snackbar under the toolbar. Set duration = clamp(2s, 55ms × chars, 6s), pause on hover, add an exit animation and role=status aria-live=polite.

issues.where: shell.css:867 (body.sidebar-closed #sidebar {display:none}); sidebar.js:95-101; shell.css:869-871 (traffic-space width flips 8↔80)
issues.problem: The sidebar snaps in and out and the tab strip jumps, while the AI panel next to it slides smoothly.
issues.fix: Mirror the panel technique: transition the width 244→0 with fixed-width inner content translated and faded, and let the page follow through the slot ResizeObserver (see the animation plan).

issues.where: shell.css:193 (pop = translateY(+3px) for every menu), 405-411 (.popover), 923-927 (.sb-menu); ai-panel.js:281-285, 964, 972; panel-extras.js:36-39; sidebar.js:241-253
issues.problem: Every menu rises from below, even menus that drop down from the header (#chat-menu, .sb-menu). All of them disappear instantly through `hidden`.
issues.fix: Use directional keyframes (menu-down / menu-up) with a matching transform-origin and a shared close helper that plays a 100ms exit before setting hidden.

issues.where: shell.css:124 (.tab:hover #151516), 125 (.tab.active var(--field) #18181b)
issues.problem: Hover and active backgrounds differ by about 3/255, so a hovered background tab looks selected. The hover color is also a literal.
issues.fix: Use hover = color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 5%, transparent). Use active = var(--surface-3) plus inset hairline plus `0 1px 2px` shadow (light theme: white plus shadow).

issues.where: renderer/pages/error.html:7-14 (inline styles; h1 keeps Instrument Serif from pages.css:30 but at 24px), 22 (single retry button)
issues.problem: The serif at 24px reads inconsistently with the other pages. There is no secondary action (Back, or search for the URL), and Retry gives no pending feedback.

issues.where: shell.css:344-350 (width transition); shell.js:36-43 (ResizeObserver → IPC per frame); main/tabs.js:461-474 (setBounds)
issues.problem: Opening or closing the panel resizes the native page on every frame for 380ms. Heavy pages (Docs, YouTube, Figma) re-layout each frame and may stutter.
issues.fix: Measure first. If it stutters, use a 'reserve then slide' variant: set the slot to its final width in one step, slide only the panel contents (transform and opacity), and on close slide out first, then expand the slot once on transitionend.

issues.where: settings.css:2,5 (accent-color #eee on radios/checks) vs history.css:56, welcome.css:61, lists.css:41 (accent-color var(--accent))
issues.problem: Radios and checkboxes in Settings are white while every other page uses the accent color.
issues.fix: Set `accent-color: var(--accent)` globally in tokens.css.

animations.current: A new tab element is inserted at full width with no animation, and the tabs next to it jump to make room.
animations.proposal: Use FLIP and animate only transform and opacity. Before mutating, record each existing tab's left position. After inserting, animate shifted tabs from translateX(oldLeft-newLeft) to 0 over 180ms with var(--ease-out). The new tab animates from {opacity:0, transform:'translateY(6px) scale(.96)'} to none over 180ms --ease-out, and its .fav/.title follow 40ms later. Width stays at its final value from the start (no width tween). Reduced motion: opacity only, 100ms.

animations.current: The element is removed instantly, the remaining tabs widen, and the next tab's X shifts away from the cursor.
animations.proposal: Place an absolutely positioned ghost clone at the old rect and fade it to opacity 0 with scale(.94) over 120ms using var(--ease-in), then remove it. Siblings FLIP over 180ms --ease-out. Add Chrome's width lock: when a tab is closed with the mouse, set the remaining tabs' flex-basis to their current px widths until pointerleave on #tabstrip, then release with a 200ms FLIP, so repeated clicks on X keep hitting the next tab.

animations.current: The dragged tab follows the pointer and siblings shift with a 160ms transform, which is good. On drop all transforms reset before the IPC reorder, so the tab snaps back for a frame and then jumps.
animations.proposal: Lift on drag start: scale(1.02), a deeper shadow and z-index, over 120ms. On drop, reorder the DOM locally, FLIP every tab from its current visual x to 0 over 200ms --ease-out, then send tab:move. Keep sibling shifts at 160ms. Later, a tear-off threshold (|dy|>30px) can show a ghost preview.

animations.current: The native page view swaps instantly, and the tab background and color crossfade over 140ms.
animations.proposal: Keep the page swap instant: Chrome does the same, and any fade would need capturePage snapshots. Add press feedback `.tab:active:not(.active){transform:scale(.98)}` at 90ms and make the active treatment more distinct (see the issues). Tighten the crossfade to 120ms --ease-out. Do not animate the favicon on switch.

animations.current: There is no progress indicator, only a spinning ring in place of the favicon, which swaps abruptly when loading ends.
animations.proposal: Add a 2px accent bar inset along the bottom edge of #omnibox (inside its radius), driven by `transform: scaleX(var(--p))` with transform-origin left. Main emits progress from real signals: did-start-loading → .1, did-navigate → .35, dom-ready → .7, did-stop-loading → 1. Between signals, trickle toward .85 with a long transition (6s cubic-bezier(.1,.6,.2,1)). On done: scaleX(1) in 150ms, then opacity 0 over 200ms after a 100ms delay, then reset with transition:none. Swap spinner to favicon with a 150ms opacity crossfade plus scale(.8→1) using --ease-spring. Reduced motion: no trickle, opacity fades only.

animations.current: The ring and background transition over 140ms. The lock and search icons swap instantly through innerHTML.
animations.proposal: Keep the 140ms ring but draw it with #omnibox::after (static inset shadow) and animate opacity. Crossfade the site icon over 120ms (outgoing opacity→0 and scale .9, incoming from .9 to 1). On blur, fade the URL text color var(--text)→var(--text-2) over 120ms. Do not animate the text content.

animations.current: The card's 160ms `in` animation plays only the first time. Rows re-render on each keystroke, the keyboard selection jumps, a hover row is highlighted alongside it, and close is instant.
animations.proposal: Restart the entrance on each new show (not on result updates): opacity 0→1 and translateY(-4px)→0 over 140ms --ease-out, origin top. When results change, crossfade rows over 80ms (opacity only). Use one `.sel-pill` element moved with translateY(index × 38px) over 90ms --ease-out, with mousemove driving the same selection. Exit over 90ms (opacity) through a two-phase hide in main: send `overlay-out`, remove after 100ms unless shown again. Reduced motion: no translate.

animations.current: This works well. The panel width animates 380ms open / 280ms close with --slide (cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)), the contents translate 28px and fade with a 30-50ms stagger, and reduced motion is respected. The page is resized on every frame through the ResizeObserver.
animations.proposal: Keep the curve and the stagger. Rename the tokens to --dur-page and --ease-drawer. theme.summary:
Lumio is dark-only and has no theme switch today. Nothing uses nativeTheme (grep finds zero hits). Colors come from two separate token roots with different names: shell.css:3-33 has 21 color tokens plus `color-scheme: dark`, and pages.css:3-9 has 15, using `--line2` and `--card2` where the shell uses `--line-strong`. Neither root is used consistently. There are about 410 hex/rgba color literals in renderer CSS, and about 320 of them would need tokens. Most are translucent white overlays (#ffffffNN, about 65), dark surface hexes (about 85) and accent tints hardcoded as #86b7ffNN (about 35). Those accent tints already ignore the profile accent today, which is a bug. overlay.css (the omnibox, downloads, site-info, account, autofill, passkey, update and screenshare popups) has its own gray scale with about 88 literals and only `--accent` as a token.

Native colors are fixed literals in four places. main/window.js:59-60 sets the window background and the Windows title bar overlay. main/tabs.js:88 and :165 set the tab view background: '#0c0c0d' for lumio: pages and '#ffffff' for web pages. main/main.js:484 sets the checkout window background.

The accent comes from THEME_COLORS (icons.js:73, copied in settings.js:7). These are pastels tuned for dark backgrounds. On white, blue is about 2.1:1, green about 1.5:1 and mono about 1.2:1, so they are unreadable as text or links.

Internal pages only have `lumioPage.invoke` (preload/internal.js:14-18), with no push events. So the cleanest approach is to drive everything from `nativeTheme.themeSource`, which feeds CSS `prefers-color-scheme` in every webContents live. Single-definition tokens would use `light-dark()` under `color-scheme: light dark`; Chromium has supported that since M123.

Incognito needs a forced-dark attribute injected by the lumio:// protocol handler. The shell and overlay share the default session with normal windows, so they would get it through a query flag. Each incognito tab session already registers its own pages handler (main.js:105-113), so a forceDark option there covers incognito internal pages.

Name the new setting `appearance` ('system' | 'light' | 'dark') and the root attribute `data-appearance`. `profile.theme` already means the accent name, settings.js:107/118 uses `data-theme` on swatches together with `closest('[data-theme]')`, and account.e2e.mjs:236/239 depends on both.

`color-scheme: dark` at shell.css:32, pages.css:8 and settings.css:128 forces dark native scrollbars, selects and date pickers. It needs to become `light dark`, plus a forced value under [data-appearance].

lumio:// handler. The shell, overlay and aura are served from the default session, which normal and incognito windows share. Each tab session, including each incognito session (incognitoProfile, main.js:110-113), registers its own page handler. This is where a forced-dark `data-appearance` attribute can be added to the HTML before first paint, without an inline script (the CSP is script-src 'self').

Internal pages only get lumioPage.invoke, with no events. The shell event list (EVENTS) has no theme event. Internal pages should therefore follow prefers-color-scheme rather than IPC. Add an 'appearance' event to the shell's EVENTS only if JS-drawn colors need it.

DEFAULT_SETTINGS has no appearance key, and profile.theme already means the accent name. setProfile validates THEMES. page:settings and page:set-setting are where a validated 'appearance' key goes. The synced SETTINGS list decides whether appearance syncs.

plan: 1. Create one shared token file, renderer/assets/theme.css. It is reachable from every lumio:// host because protocol.js:57-60 serves /assets/* for all of them. Import it at the top of shell.css, overlay.css and pages.css, the way fonts.css is imported today. Layer A is a base palette: a neutral ramp (0-1000) and blue, purple, green, amber, red and pink ramps. Layer B is semantic tokens, each defined once with light-dark(light, dark): --bg, --chrome, --sidebar, --panel, --card, --card2, --field, --field-hover, --field-focus, --hover, --active, --line, --line-strong (keep --line2 as an alias for the pages), --text, --dim, --label, --overlay-1..4 (replacing #ffffff06/0a/10/14/1f/24 with black alpha in light), --scrim, --shadow-sm/md/lg (softer in light), --slot-bg, --code-bg, --bubble, --primary-bg/-fg/-hover (inverted in light: #18181b on #fafafa), --on-accent, --accent-soft/-line (color-mix of var(--accent)), --danger/-text/-soft, --ok/-text, --warn/-text, --star, --switch-off, --shimmer-lo/-hi. Root rules: `:root{color-scheme:light dark}`, `:root[data-appearance=dark]{color-scheme:dark}`, `:root[data-appearance=light]{color-scheme:light}`. Electron 43's Chromium supports light-dark() and color-mix(). The fallback, if needed, is the same tokens duplicated under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light){:root:not([data-appearance=dark]){…}}`.

2. Suggested light values: bg/chrome #f3f3f5, sidebar #ebebee, panel/card #ffffff, card2 #fafafa, field #e8e8eb, field-hover #e1e1e5, hover #00000008, active #00000012, line #00000014, line-strong #00000024, text #18181b, dim #52525b, label #6b6b73 (at least 4.5:1 on white), slot-bg #ffffff, danger #c5221f, ok #137333, warn #b06000. Keep today's dark values exactly so dark mode does not change visually.

Dark surfaces become semantic tokens. Pastel status text becomes the matching *-text token. #0b0b0c on accent fills becomes --on-accent. The shimmer at shell.css:474 uses --shimmer tokens. notice.info at shell.css:515 mixes with var(--text) instead of #fff. Order by size: shell.css (~110), overlay.css (~88, replace its whole gray scale), settings.css (~32; radio accent-color and the swatch ring become var(--text)), newtab.css (~14), welcome.css (~14), history.css (10), pages.css (9; delete its :root block), passwords.css (6), lists.css (5). Leave aura.css, the masks, brand chips, the update button, the slider starfield and page-scripts fixed. Then add a node test that greps renderer CSS and JS for hex/rgba outside theme.css, with an allowlist, so new literals cannot slip in.

4. JS colors. Turn THEME_COLORS into { id: { dark, light } } in a shared /assets/theme-colors.js, imported by shell.js, overlay.js and settings.js, which removes the copy at settings.js:6-7. Suggested light accents: blue #2563eb, purple #7c3aed, green #15803d, orange #c2410c, pink #db2777, mono #27272a. Incognito keeps #b58cff on its forced-dark root. applyTheme (shell.js:530) and settings.js:108 set --accent-d and --accent-l, and theme.css defines `--accent: light-dark(var(--accent-l), var(--accent-d))`. Send the accent id rather than the computed --accent to the overlay (shell.js:316/552/592, overlay.js:218). Replace the hardcoded SVG strokes: newtab.js:4 and welcome.js:8 become currentColor plus var(--accent), extensions.js:5 becomes currentColor. Replace the inline #7c7c80 at overlay.js:17 with a class. In light mode, darken agent dots in CSS (shell.css:821-826).

5. Add the setting. In main/store.js DEFAULT_SETTINGS add `appearance: 'system'`. Do not call it 'theme', because profile.theme, the settings swatches' data-theme and the e2e selectors already use that name. In main.js whenReady, right after `store = new Store(...)` (main.js:1226) and before any window or view exists, set `nativeTheme.themeSource = store.settings.appearance`. Add setAppearance(v), which validates the value against ['system','light','dark'], saves it and sets themeSource. Handle the 'appearance' key in page:set-setting (main.js:1021) and return it from page:settings (main.js:952). Decide whether to add it to the synced keys in sync/adapters.js:11; Chrome does sync themes. If it syncs, call setAppearance in onApplied.

6. Settings UI. In the Appearance card (settings.html:266-277), add a 'Theme' row with a three-way segmented control, System / Light / Dark, each with a mini preview thumbnail. Reuse the .modes radio styles (settings.css:1-5). Wire it up next to settings.js:392. Optionally add a View → Appearance radio submenu in menu.js (View section 71-90) and in the ⋮ browser menu (menu.js:138+).

7. Native colors. Add main/theme.js with isDark(incognito) = incognito || nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors, and colors(dark) returning { frame: dark ? '#070708' : '#f3f3f5', internal: dark ? '#0c0c0d' : '#ffffff', symbol: dark ? '#a8a8a8' : '#5f5f66' }. Use it in window.js:59-60 (this also fixes the #080808 vs #070708 mismatch), in tabs.js:88/165 (TabManager already knows `incognito`) and in the main.js:484 checkout window. Register nativeTheme.on('updated'), which fires on setting changes and on OS changes in system mode. For every alive window, call win.setBackgroundColor and, on win32, win.setTitleBarOverlay. For every tab whose URL starts with lumio:, call view.setBackgroundColor. The CSS of the shell, overlay and internal pages updates by itself through prefers-color-scheme.

In protocol.js makeHandler, for .html responses whose request query has appearance=dark, rewrite `<html lang="en">` to include `data-appearance="dark"`. Give registerPagesProtocol a { forceDark } option and pass true from incognitoProfile (main.js:110-113), so every incognito internal page (newtab, settings, history and so on) is served pre-darkened. Check that the preload's `location.href.startsWith('lumio://shell/')` check and the permission check at main.js:1238 still match with a query string; they do. Keep the body.incognito overrides (shell.css:73-84, newtab.css:55-57) on top. Accept that the macOS traffic lights and context menus in incognito follow the app appearance, because Electron has no per-window NSAppearance.

Re-check the panel, chat-full gradient (383), popovers with backdrop blur (408, 925; use translucent white in light), user bubble (443), code and pre (457-458, 506), thinking shimmer (473-476), plan step icons (560-567), composer (575-579), model, mode and bypass menus (594, 664-672), slider (608-621), chips and page-suggest (644-654), attachments (738-746), usage ring and popover (750-761), made images (772), voice bar and orb (790-817), helpers (821-843), workflow card (846-854), and marked-rendered tables and links. risks: Contrast. --label #76767e and the pastel status texts (#ffb4a8, #ffc98f, #ff9b9b, #bff1d3, #cfe0ff, #d6c2ff, #ffd479, #f0b36b) fail on white and each needs its own light value. About 65 #ffffff06-24 overlays and dividers disappear on white and must flip to black alpha. Shadows tuned for black (#000c, #0008, 0 18px 50px) look muddy on light.

Load flashes. The lumio: tab view background '#0c0c0d' (tabs.js:88/165) flashes dark before newtab paints in light mode. The window background '#080808' shows on resize. body.incognito is applied only after the async shell:init (shell.js:706), so the forced dark has to come from the protocol injection, not JS. A theme switch fires many color transitions at once.

Naming collisions. profile.theme is the accent name. settings.js:107 puts data-theme on swatches and settings.js:118 uses closest('[data-theme]'), which would match an <html data-theme> and send 'dark' as an accent; main.js:579 rejects it, but it is sloppy. account.e2e.mjs:236 clicks [data-theme=green]. Use `appearance` and `data-appearance`.

nativeTheme.themeSource is app-global. It also flips websites' prefers-color-scheme, which matches Chrome's Appearance setting, along with native menus, dialogs, notifications and the traffic lights. Incognito windows in light mode will get light context menus and traffic lights next to a dark UI, because Electron has no per-window appearance API.

A custom property set to light-dark() keeps its unresolved string in getComputedStyle. Code that reads --accent (shell.js:316/552/592 into overlay.js:218, and account.e2e.mjs:239) will receive 'light-dark(...)'. Pass ids instead, or register @property --accent { syntax: '<color>' }.

Volume and missed states. About 320 literals across 10 CSS files, with overlay.css carrying a full parallel gray palette. Hover, selected and disabled states in rarely opened popups (passkey, screenshare, update card, site-info select, schedule date pickers) are easy to miss. A grep-based guard test and light screenshots of every overlay kind are needed.

Windows title bar. The titleBarOverlay symbolColor '#a8a8a8' and color '#080808' are static, so the caption buttons will look wrong on a light tab strip until setTitleBarOverlay runs on every theme update.
Test determinism. With 'system' as the default, e2e screenshots and any color assertions depend on the CI runner's OS appearance unless tests pin the appearance.
Sync. If appearance joins sync/adapters.js:11 SETTINGS, one device's choice overrides the others. A 'system' value is safe; a forced value may surprise people.

Out of scope. The aura and page-scripts glow and the Stop pill stay fixed. The phone companion (mobile/, server /companion), the website, the Stripe and checkout pages, the built-in PDF viewer, DevTools and extension popups theme themselves.

gaps.approach: Tabs: renderTabs (shell.js:93-105) inserts and removes DOM instantly. Add FLIP: grow new tabs from width 0 with an opacity fade, and shrink closing tabs before removing them. Chrome's close-in-a-row behavior: freeze tab widths while the pointer is inside #tabs and relayout on pointerleave. Give tab drag a spring settle instead of the plain 160ms transform (shell.css:147-148). Overlay dropdowns (omnibox suggestions, downloads, account, site info) only fade 4px (overlay.css:17): use scale(.98)+opacity from the anchor's transform-origin with a staggered row reveal and an exit animation before hideOverlay (window.js hideOverlay removes the view instantly, so animate out and then remove). Find bar (shell.html:31-37), permission infobar (shell.html:56-61) and bookmarks bar show/hide need height/transform transitions. Also animate the omnibox icon slots (star, key, zoom) and the toast. Use transform/opacity only, add a shared --spring easing token, and honor prefers-reduced-motion everywhere plus a future Energy Saver flag. WebContentsViews can't be CSS-animated, so animate shell chrome around them and never step setBounds per frame.

gaps.feature: Tear-off tabs / drag tabs between windows
gaps.approach: startTabDrag (shell.js:107-151) clamps the drag to the strip. When the pointer leaves the strip vertically (>40px), send 'tab:drag-out'. Main detaches the tab (tabs.js:249) and creates a BrowserWin with adopt (as moveTabToNewWindow does, main.js:273-279), then moves that window with the cursor (poll screen.getCursorScreenPoint until mouseup). The view moves without reloading. Each shell reports its #tabs rect in screen coordinates. On drop over another window's strip, adopt into that window at the computed index; otherwise keep the new window. Handle extensions removeTab/addTab as moveTabToNewWindow does.

gaps.approach: No 'update-target-url' handler exists. In tabs.js wire() (:140), listen for wc.on('update-target-url') and emit it to the window. gaps.feature: 'Leave site?' beforeunload dialog
gaps.approach: There is no will-prevent-unload handler for user tabs (the only one is main/ai/tools/web.js:38). With Electron's default, a page's beforeunload silently cancels reload or navigation with no prompt. Closing a tab skips beforeunload entirely (tabs.js:284 calls webContents.close() without waitForBeforeUnload), so unsaved form text is lost. Fix: call wc.close({waitForBeforeUnload:true}) and remove the tab only on 'destroyed'. In wire(), handle 'will-prevent-unload' with dialog.showMessageBoxSync(win, {message:'Leave site?', buttons:['Leave','Cancel']}) and call e.preventDefault() on Leave. Window close (window.js close handler) should do the same per tab.

gaps.feature: JavaScript dialogs: window.prompt support and tab-modal alert/confirm
gaps.approach: Electron does not implement window.prompt() (it returns null), and alert/confirm are app-modal native boxes without the origin or a 'prevent more dialogs' option. In preload/internal.js, use contextBridge.executeInMainWorld (or webFrame.executeJavaScript) to override prompt (and optionally alert/confirm) with a synchronous ipcRenderer.sendSync to main. Main shows a tab-modal overlay (new 'jsdialog' kind in overlay.js) labeled with the page origin and blocks until answered, with suppression per tab after 3 dialogs.

gaps.feature: Pop-up blocker with omnibox 'blocked' icon and per-site allow
gaps.approach: setWindowOpenHandler (tabs.js:212-231) allows every window.open: sized popups become windows and foreground-tab dispositions create tabs, even without a user gesture, so spam sites can open tabs freely. Track the last user input per webContents with wc.on('input-event') (mouseDown/keyDown/touch timestamps). In the handler, deny when there was no input in the last ~1s and the site isn't allowed (sitePermissions[origin].popups). Push the blocked URLs to the shell, which shows an omnibox icon. A new overlay kind lists the blocked pop-ups with 'Always allow pop-ups and redirects from <site>' and Open.

gaps.feature: Certificate error interstitial ('Your connection is not private' + Proceed)
gaps.approach: No 'certificate-error' handler exists, so bad-cert sites just show the generic error page (error.js:5-23) with no way through. Handle app.on('certificate-error', (e, wc, url, error, cert, cb)): e.preventDefault(), cb(false), and load lumio://error/?code=cert&err=...&url= with an 'Advanced' expander showing the error code and cert subject/issuer and a 'Proceed to host (unsafe)'. Proceeding adds host+fingerprint to an in-memory allow set and reloads; the next certificate-error for that pair calls cb(true). Mark the omnibox 'Not secure' red for that tab.

gaps.approach: Add a setting clearOnExit plus keep-list origins. In before-quit (main.js:1415-1421), await normal.session.clearStorageData (per origin excluding exceptions: list cookies via session.cookies.get and remove those not in the keep-list).

gaps.feature: Built-in ad & tracker blocking (differentiator)
gaps.approach: Add @ghostery/adblocker-electron with EasyList+EasyPrivacy (cached in userData, refreshed daily). Enable it on the normal and incognito sessions, with per-site toggles in the site info popover and a blocked-count badge. Make sure it doesn't conflict with the extensions' webRequest use (main/extensions.js).

gaps.feature: Safety check page
gaps.approach: A Settings > Privacy card that runs: update status (updater.state), compromised/weak passwords (Checkup), extensions with MV2 or a blocklist hit, Safe Browsing/blocklist on, unused site permissions (timestamped grants), and notification-spam sites. Each item links to its fix.

gaps.feature: Site data viewer (cookies and storage per site)
gaps.approach: The site info popover can only clear data (main.js:797-815). Show cookie and site counts (session.cookies.get({domain})), storage usage via CDP Storage.getUsageAndQuota through webContents.debugger, and a per-site list in Settings with delete.

gaps.feature: Per-site content toggles (JavaScript, images, insecure content, automatic downloads)
gaps.approach: javascript and images are webPreferences fixed at view creation (tabs.js:76-85). When a site's setting changes, recreate the tab's view with the right prefs (swap the views keeping history via navigationHistory.restore), or inject a CSP header via webRequest.onHeadersReceived (script-src 'none'). Pop-ups, sound and downloads are handled in our own handlers.

gaps.feature: Device choosers (USB, HID, Serial, Bluetooth) and File System Access permission
gaps.approach: The check and request handlers deny 'usb', 'hid', 'serial', 'fileSystem' and 'storage-access' (features.js:137-138,168-177), so WebUSB, WebHID, Web Serial, Web Bluetooth and showSaveFilePicker write access fail. Add session.on('select-usb-device'|'select-hid-device'|'select-serial-port') and wc.on('select-bluetooth-device') with a chooser overlay, plus setDevicePermissionHandler, and make 'fileSystem' askable.

gaps.feature: Geolocation on Windows
gaps.approach: The permission is askable (features.js:137), but on Windows Electron may fall back to Google's network location provider, which needs GOOGLE_API_KEY. Test it, then enable the WinRT system location provider via a Chromium feature switch, or supply a key. macOS needs NSLocationUsageDescription in the Info.plist in build/package.mjs.

gaps.feature: Preferred camera/microphone and per-site device switch
gaps.approach: Add Settings selects populated from navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices in the settings page. preload/internal.js wraps getUserMedia constraints in the main world to set deviceId for the preferred device. The site info popover offers a device switch.

gaps.feature: Extensions UX: pin/unpin toolbar icons, per-site access, Details (allow in incognito, file URLs), Errors, keyboard shortcuts page, extensions in incognito
gaps.approach: The puzzle button only opens the manager (shell.js:605-606). Replace it with an overlay listing extensions with pin toggles. Feed the pinned set into <browser-action-list> filtering, and add 'This can read and change site data' controls (on click / on site / all sites, enforced via webRequest host checks). Add a Details view to extensions.html, a chrome.commands shortcuts page, and opt-in incognito by loading allowed extensions into the incognito session too.

gaps.feature: Memory Saver modes, 'Always keep these sites active' list, memory saved; Energy Saver
gaps.approach: discard/sleepIdle (tabs.js:111-138) is time-based only. Add an exceptions list checked in discard(), and Moderate/Balanced/Maximum modes that map to minutes plus a memory-pressure trigger (app.getAppMetrics total). Track bytes freed per discard for the hover card. Energy Saver: powerMonitor 'on-battery'/'on-ac' toggles body.energy-saver (disables UI animations) and wc.setBackgroundThrottling plus CDP Page.setWebLifecycleState('frozen') for background tabs.

gaps.feature: Task Manager (Shift+Esc)
gaps.approach: Add lumio://taskmanager (or a small BrowserWindow) polling app.getAppMetrics() every second and mapping PIDs to tabs (wc.getOSProcessId()), extensions (background pages), GPU and utility processes. Show memory, CPU and network (count bytes via webRequest.onCompleted per wc), with End process via wc.forcefullyCrashRenderer().

gaps.feature: Performance issue alerts
gaps.approach: Poll app.getAppMetrics() every 30s, flag tabs above CPU/memory thresholds, and show a toolbar chip offering to sleep them via discard().

gaps.feature: Preload pages (preconnect / prerender omnibox suggestions)
gaps.approach: Call session.preconnect({url, numSockets:1}) for the top omnibox suggestion as the user types and for NTP shortcuts on hover. Leave full prerender for later (it needs a hidden WebContentsView swap).

gaps.feature: Back/forward cache
gaps.approach: No feature switches are set (grep for appendSwitch found nothing). Test app.commandLine.appendSwitch('enable-features','BackForwardCache') on Electron 43 and measure the back/forward speed and stability in e2e tests before shipping it.

gaps.feature: Customize panel: NTP background, custom color themes (tonal palettes), toolbar customization, show/hide toggles (home, full URLs), UI density
gaps.approach: Only six accent colors exist (icons.js:73, settings.html:61-84). Add a 'Customize Lumio' side panel with live preview. NTP background: upload (stored in userData), bundled collections, or a solid color. A custom color picker generates light and dark tonal palettes with @material/material-color-utilities into the CSS tokens. Toolbar pin/unpin for home, forward, reading mode, translate, print, task manager, copy link, with drag to arrange. Add 'Always show full URLs' (prettyUrl in shell.js:166-170) and compact/comfortable density via CSS variables.

gaps.feature: Font settings and default font size
gaps.approach: Add Settings > Appearance > Font size (preset) and Customize fonts (standard/serif/sans/fixed, minimum size). Apply them as webPreferences defaultFontSize, defaultFontFamily and minimumFontSize in ensureView (tabs.js:76-85). They apply to new tabs, or recreate the views to apply now.

gaps.feature: Force dark mode for web pages
gaps.approach: Test --enable-features=WebContentsForceDark (set before ready). Otherwise inject a Dark Reader-style stylesheet via wc.insertCSS when enabled.

gaps.feature: Import from Firefox; import search engines/autofill; Chromium passwords on Windows; keep bookmark folders
gaps.approach: Add main/importer/firefox.js reading profiles.ini → places.sqlite (copy it first, it's locked; use node:sqlite as chromium.js does for History) for bookmarks with folders and history. Decrypt Windows Chromium passwords with Local State os_crypt.encrypted_key via DPAPI (a native helper in main/win or PowerShell ProtectedData) plus AES-GCM. Read Chrome 'Web Data' keywords for search engines.

gaps.feature: Send tab to your devices
gaps.approach: Lumio Sync already lists devices and open tabs (main/sync/engine.js). Add a 'sent tabs' encrypted record type and an omnibox/share/context menu 'Send to <device>'. The receiving desktop shows a Notification that opens the tab, and the phone companion gets a push (main/sync/companion.js).

gaps.feature: Sync more data types (reading list, tab groups, passkeys, extensions list, themes, addresses)
gaps.approach: Add adapters in main/sync/adapters.js as each feature lands (reading list, saved groups, passkeys from main/passkeys.js, an installed extension ID list to reinstall from the Web Store, the theme/customize settings), plus toggles in settings.html:87-126.

gaps.feature: Share menu (macOS Share sheet, Copy link) and QR code generator
gaps.approach: Add an omnibox share icon and the ⋮ 'Cast, save and share' entry. Copy link, a QR code (bundle the qrcode lib, Lumio mark in the center, Copy/Download) in an overlay, and on Mac new ShareMenu({urls:[url]}).popup(). Also put QR code on link and image context menus.

gaps.feature: Screenshot tool (visible area, region, full page; copy/download/annotate)
gaps.approach: Capture the visible area with wc.capturePage(rect). For the full page, wc.debugger.sendCommand('Page.captureScreenshot', {captureBeyondViewport:true}). Region select via a transparent overlay WebContentsView over the slot, then copy (clipboard.writeImage), save, annotate in a small editor, or 'Ask Lumio about this' (the AI vision alternative to Lens).

gaps.feature: Install site as app / Create shortcut
gaps.approach: Read the web app manifest (preload/internal.js finds <link rel=manifest>). 'Install' opens an app-style BrowserWindow (no tab strip, own session partition shared with the profile) and creates OS launchers: Windows .lnk with --app=<url> via shell.writeShortcutLink; on Mac, a small generated .app wrapper that runs Lumio with --app.

gaps.feature: Help center and 'Report an issue' (Alt+Shift+I) with optional screenshot/URL/system info
gaps.approach: Add a Help submenu in menu.js and ⋮. 'Report an issue' opens an overlay form (description, opt-in screenshot via the existing snapshot() in main.js:1424-1453, opt-in URL, version and OS) that POSTs to the Lumio Worker.

gaps.feature: Quit / close warnings (hold Cmd+Q, close window with many tabs)
gaps.approach: Replace role 'quit' (menu.js:28) with a custom item that shows a 'Hold ⌘Q to quit' overlay and quits after ~1s held (watch keyUp via before-input-event), with a setting. In window.js 'close', confirm when the window has more than N tabs.

gaps.feature: Dock menu, Windows Jump List and taskbar integration
gaps.approach: At ready: app.dock.setMenu(Menu with New Window / New Incognito Window) on Mac. On Windows, app.setUserTasks([{program: process.execPath, arguments:'--new-window'}, '--incognito']) and parse the args in launchTargets/second-instance (main.js:57-68, 1219-1223).

gaps.feature: Crash reporting (opt-in)
gaps.approach: Call crashReporter.start({submitURL: Lumio Worker or Sentry minidump endpoint, uploadToServer: settings.crashReports}) before ready, and add a Settings toggle.

gaps.feature: System settings: hardware acceleration toggle, proxy, continue running in background (Windows lifecycle)
gaps.approach: Hardware acceleration: a stored flag read synchronously before ready → app.disableHardwareAcceleration(), with a relaunch button (app.relaunch). Proxy: open OS proxy settings, or session.setProxy for custom/PAC. gaps.feature: Preferred languages (Accept-Language) and browser UI language (i18n EN/ES)

gaps.feature: Omnibox: Switch to tab, @tabs/@bookmarks/@history/@lumio scopes, Chrome-style Actions

Mark matches that are already open and render a 'Switch to this tab' button in renderSuggest (overlay.js:12-22); on pick, focus that window and tab. '@scope' + Space filters the providers (@lumio → Ask Lumio). Add a static action list ('clear browsing data', 'manage passwords', 'update browser', 'incognito') matched by keywords and shown as an action row.

gaps.feature: Omnibox details: paste and go, Shift+Delete remove suggestion, Alt/Shift/Ctrl+Enter modifiers, calculator/unit answers
gaps.approach: Add a custom contextmenu on #address with 'Paste and go' / 'Paste and search for “…”'. Shift+Delete on a history row calls store.deleteHistory for that URL. Alt+Enter opens a new tab, Shift+Enter a new window, and Ctrl+Enter adds www/.com (Lumio currently uses Cmd/Ctrl+Enter for a new tab, shell.js:235-255). Add a math/unit evaluator row (a small safe parser, no eval) at the top of suggest().

gaps.feature: Lookalike / IDN spoofing protection

gaps.feature: Error pages polish: error codes/Details, auto-reload when back online, offline mini-game

gaps.feature: Live Caption (and translated captions)

Capture tab audio (desktopCapturer loopback on Windows, or wc audio via a getDisplayMedia self-capture), stream it to Lumio's STT (voice.js already streams mic audio through mic-worklet.js), and render captions in a draggable overlay view. gaps.feature: Name window
gaps.approach: Add Window > Name Window… with a small overlay input that stores w.name, sets win.setTitle(name), and saves it in the session.

gaps.approach: Render the same tab state into the left sidebar (renderer/ui/sidebar.js already exists) when settings.verticalTabs is on, hide #tabs, and reuse the drag/groups logic. A good differentiator alongside tab groups.

gaps.feature: Privacy extras: Do Not Track / GPC, WebRTC IP handling policy, auto-revoke unused permissions

WebRTC: wc.setWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy('default_public_interface_only') in ensureView when the setting is on. Auto-revoke: add a lastVisit per origin in sitePermissions and expire grants after 90 days, with a Safety check notice.

gaps.feature: Protocol handlers (navigator.registerProtocolHandler)
gaps.approach: Polyfill registerProtocolHandler in the main world through the preload. Store handlers (scheme → URL template) after a prompt, and route mailto:/web+ links to them in the openExternal flow before falling back to the OS.

gaps.feature: PDF handling setting (download PDFs vs open in viewer)

gaps.feature: Keyboard shortcut customization

Map chrome://gpu and media-internals to the content-layer pages if Electron serves them.

Add 'Help me write' in the editable context menu (tabs.js:571-582) that opens a mini composer.

notPossible.feature: Cast tab / screen / media to Chromecast and Google TV
notPossible.why: Chrome's Media Router and Cast stack and the Presentation API are not in Electron, and Cast receivers expect Google's sender framework.
notPossible.alternative: Leave Cast out at launch. Later, offer a castv2 library for plain media URLs only, or point Mac users to AirPlay screen mirroring.

notPossible.feature: Web Push notifications when the tab is closed (pushManager.subscribe)
notPossible.why: Chrome delivers push through Google's FCM/GCM. Electron has no push service, so subscribe() fails.
notPossible.alternative: Notifications from open tabs still work. Pinned tabs, background mode with a tray icon, and the Lumio companion push for Lumio's own events. List it as a known limitation.

notPossible.feature: Website speech recognition (webkitSpeechRecognition)
notPossible.why: Chrome streams the audio to Google's speech servers, which Electron can't use.
notPossible.alternative: Polyfill webkitSpeechRecognition in the main world with Lumio's own STT (renderer/ui/voice.js pipeline).

notPossible.feature: Google account browser sign-in and Chrome Sync
notPossible.why: Google's sync and sign-in endpoints are only for Chrome.
notPossible.alternative: Lumio account plus Lumio Sync with end-to-end encryption (already built).

notPossible.feature: Safe Browsing Enhanced protection (and free commercial use of Google Safe Browsing)
notPossible.why: Enhanced protection is Google-only, and the free Safe Browsing API is for non-commercial use.
notPossible.alternative: Paid Google Web Risk API through the Lumio Worker, or open blocklists (URLhaus, OpenPhish, PhishTank) with Lumio's own interstitial.

notPossible.feature: Google Lens (overlay and region search)
notPossible.why: There's no official Lens API, and region uploads use private endpoints.
notPossible.alternative: Open lens.google.com/uploadbyurl for public image URLs, and add 'Ask Lumio about this' on a region screenshot with Lumio's AI vision.

notPossible.feature: Chrome's built-in Translate (Google service or on-device model)
notPossible.why: The translate infrastructure and models are in the Chrome layer and use Google's service.
notPossible.alternative: Lumio translation through the Worker (LLM, or DeepL/Cloud Translate with Lumio's own key) injected into DOM text nodes.

notPossible.feature: Gemini in Chrome and Gemini Nano on-device features (scam detection, Help me write on-device)
notPossible.why: Gemini Nano and the Chrome AI integration are not shipped in Electron.
notPossible.alternative: Lumio AI (already the assistant), with server-side checks only if the user opts in.

notPossible.feature: Live Caption with Google's SODA model
notPossible.why: The SODA speech model is a Google component downloaded only by Chrome.
notPossible.alternative: Capture tab audio and caption it with Lumio's STT or a local Whisper model.

notPossible.feature: Enhanced spell check (Google cloud grammar)
notPossible.why: It is a Google-only service.
notPossible.alternative: LanguageTool or Lumio AI 'Fix grammar and spelling' (already in the selection menu).

notPossible.feature: Google Pay, virtual cards and Chrome's Payment Request sheet
notPossible.why: The Payment Request UI is in the Chrome layer and Google Pay card provisioning is Google's.
notPossible.alternative: Sites fall back to their own or pop-up checkout. Lumio's own encrypted card autofill, later.

notPossible.feature: Extension native messaging (1Password, Bitwarden, Grammarly desktop integration)
notPossible.why: Electron doesn't implement chrome.runtime.connectNative.
notPossible.alternative: Password extensions in standalone mode, and Lumio's built-in password manager.

notPossible.feature: Privacy Sandbox ad APIs (Topics, Protected Audience, ad measurement)
notPossible.why: These are Google ad features, not meaningful outside Chrome.
notPossible.alternative: Turn the APIs off and say so in Privacy settings.

notPossible.feature: Family Link supervised profiles
notPossible.why: Family Link is Google-only.
notPossible.alternative: An optional enterprise JSON policy file for managed installs, post-launch.

notPossible.feature: Google Doodles and the Google-account New Tab Page
notPossible.why: Google content and services.
notPossible.alternative: Lumio's own NTP with backgrounds, shortcuts and AI cards.

notPossible.feature: Chrome's natural read-aloud voices
notPossible.why: Those voices are Google's cloud or on-device models.
notPossible.alternative: System speechSynthesis voices or Lumio TTS.

notPossible.feature: Hybrid passkeys (sign in with a phone via QR / caBLE)
notPossible.why: Electron doesn't expose Chromium's hybrid WebAuthn transport.
notPossible.alternative: Lumio platform passkeys synced through Lumio Sync, and approvals from the phone companion.

notPossible.feature: FedCM browser account chooser ('Sign in with…')
notPossible.why: The FedCM UI lives in the Chrome layer and is missing in Electron.
notPossible.alternative: Sites fall back to pop-up OAuth, which Lumio's popup handling supports (main/tabs.js:212-225).

notPossible.feature: Rich omnibox answers and entity suggestions from Google's private suggest response
notPossible.why: These come from Google-only suggest fields.
notPossible.alternative: Public suggest endpoints for queries, plus our own calculator/units, weather or dictionary APIs, or Lumio AI answers.

notPossible.feature: Google Shopping price tracking and shared tab groups through Google
notPossible.why: Both depend on Google backends.
notPossible.alternative: Lumio Worker features: AI price watching and shared groups through Lumio Sync, post-launch.

missedGaps.feature: Popup windows (window.open with a size, used for OAuth and payments) get no browser features: no read-only URL/lock bar, no context menu, password autofill, permission prompts, nested-popup policy or 'Open in tab'
missedGaps.why: tabs.js:217-222 returns action:'allow' with only overrideBrowserWindowOptions, and nothing hooks the new window: grep finds no 'did-create-window', 'web-contents-created' or 'browser-window-created' in main/. Consequences: (1) the user can't see which origin a sign-in or payment popup is on (Chrome shows a minimal location bar with the lock), which is a phishing risk. (2) The Permissions request handler (features.js:174-198) calls emitFor(wc.id) (main.js:131-135), which only finds tab views, so a camera, mic or notification request from a popup is never shown and stays pending. (3) password-manager.js:57/65/128 use findTab(e.sender), which returns null for popups, so autofill and save never work in popup sign-in flows. (4) Right-click does nothing because no 'context-menu' handler is attached, and the lumio:// guard (tabs.js:203-210) isn't attached either. Fix: handle 'did-create-window' and wire the child with a small popup chrome.

missedGaps.feature: macOS: opening HTML/PDF files from Finder or the Dock ('open-file')
missedGaps.why: build/package.mjs:87-89 declares CFBundleDocumentTypes public.html/public.xhtml, but main.js only handles 'open-url' (main.js:1207) and 'second-instance'. There is no app.on('open-file'), so Open With > Lumio, double-clicking an .html file when Lumio is the default, and dragging a file onto the Dock icon do nothing on Mac. PDF is registered on Windows (launchTargets main.js:57-68) but isn't declared on Mac.

missedGaps.feature: Screen share: 'Share this tab' / a single browser-tab source with tab audio
missedGaps.why: The picker only lists desktopCapturer 'screen' and 'window' sources (main.js:536). Sharing a tab with its audio is the most common choice in Meet, Zoom web and Discord, and system audio is Windows-only (main.js:566). Electron's setDisplayMediaRequestHandler callback accepts a WebFrameMain as both the video and audio source, so tab capture with audio works on Mac too. Pair it with the 'Sharing this tab / Stop' bar from the capture-indicators gap.

missedGaps.feature: Fullscreen / pointer-lock exit notice ('Press Esc to exit full screen', 'Press Esc to show your cursor')
missedGaps.why: This is a Chrome anti-spoofing UI that lives in the Chrome layer, so Electron doesn't have it. In HTML fullscreen the page view is resized to cover the whole window (tabs.js:187-193, 470-472), so the shell DOM can't show anything, and the 'fullscreen' event only toggles a body class (shell.js:684). The notice needs a transient overlay WebContentsView above the page. features.js:138 also auto-grants pointerLock with no notice.

missedGaps.feature: 'Save Link As… / Save Image As… / Save Video As…' should always show a Save dialog
missedGaps.why: tabs.js:563, 572 and 581 call wc.downloadURL(), and will-download (features.js:58-63) only shows a dialog when settings.askDownload is on. So the 'Save … As…' items silently save to Downloads, unlike Chrome. Flag downloads started from these items (e.g., a pending-URL set) and call item.setSaveDialogOptions for them.

missedGaps.feature: Window-management permission is granted to every site without asking
missedGaps.why: features.js:138 puts 'window-management' in ALWAYS, so getScreenDetails() (multi-screen layout and screen labels, a fingerprinting surface) is granted silently. Chrome prompts for it. Move it to ASKABLE with a label and add it to the Site settings lists.

missedGaps.feature: Tab strip empty-area context menu and 'Move tab to another window ›' submenu
missedGaps.why: Only .tab elements have a contextmenu listener (shell.js:66). #tabstrip has only a no-op dblclick (shell.js:154), so right-clicking the empty strip does nothing. Chrome shows New tab, Reopen closed tab, Bookmark all tabs, Name window and Task manager there. The tab menu offers only 'Move Tab to New Window' (main.js:1159), while Chrome lists the other open windows as destinations (adopt() at tabs.js:262-272 already supports this).

missedGaps.feature: Warn before quitting or closing the last window or incognito when downloads are in progress
missedGaps.why: before-quit (main.js:1415-1421) and the window 'close' handler (window.js:131) never check Downloads.items for state 'progressing'. Closing incognito wipes its partition (main.js:124-129) and quitting cancels downloads silently. Chrome shows 'N downloads in progress. Cancel downloads?' Separate from the gap's Cmd+Q-hold and many-tabs warnings.

missedGaps.feature: macOS menu bar parity (Window list, Tab menu, Bookmarks/History items, Edit > Spelling/Substitutions/Speech, View > Stop/Developer)
missedGaps.why: The Window submenu (menu.js:116-128) has only a label, no role:'window'/'windowMenu', so macOS doesn't list the open windows or provide window management items. The Bookmarks menu has only 2 commands and no bookmark items (menu.js:108-113). History shows only Recently Closed and no recently visited pages (menu.js:96-107). There is no Tab or Profiles menu. Edit lacks Spelling and Grammar, Substitutions and Speech (Electron roles exist). View lacks Stop (Cmd+.), Always Show Full URLs, Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen (Cmd+Shift+F) and a Developer submenu (View Source, JavaScript Console, Inspect). The gap analysis only adds a Help menu.

missedGaps.feature: macOS page context-menu system items: Look Up “…”, Speech, Services, Writing Tools
missedGaps.why: contextMenu (tabs.js:543-627) has no Mac-specific entries. Chrome on Mac shows Look Up (Electron: wc.showDefinitionForSelection()) and Speech > Start/Stop Speaking (roles startSpeaking/stopSpeaking) for selections and editable fields. The context-menu gap doesn't list these.

missedGaps.feature: Legal and credits pages: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, open-source licenses (chrome://credits equivalent)
missedGaps.why: grep for 'privacy policy|terms of|licenses|credits|open source' in renderer/pages/* returns nothing. For a public release of a GPL-3.0 app (package.json license) that bundles Chromium/Electron and syncs data and sends AI requests to a server, About and the welcome flow need Terms and Privacy links and a lumio://credits page with third-party notices (Electron ships LICENSES.chromium.html).

missedGaps.feature: 'Lumio isn't your default browser' infobar at startup
missedGaps.why: makeDefaultBrowser (main.js:391-403) is reachable only from the welcome flow and Settings > Default browser (settings.html:333-338). Chrome shows a dismissible 'Set as default' infobar on launch, which matters for retention after release.

missedGaps.feature: Omnibox zero-suggest on focus and 'Link you copied' clipboard suggestion
missedGaps.why: refreshSuggestions returns and hides the overlay when the text is empty (shell.js:280-283), so focusing the omnibox shows nothing. Chrome shows the most visited and recent entries (and the current URL with actions) on focus, plus a clipboard URL row. The omnibox gaps cover remote, inline and switch-to-tab suggestions but not zero-prefix ones.

missedGaps.feature: Web Share API (navigator.share) for websites
missedGaps.why: Chrome's desktop share service lives in the Chrome layer, and nothing in preload/internal.js provides it, so share buttons on sites fail. Needs verification on Electron 43. Fix: a main-world shim via the existing executeInMainWorld path (preload/internal.js:23) that calls main, which uses ShareMenu on Mac and the Windows helper (main/win) for DataTransferManager.

missedGaps.feature: Notification click / window.focus() should bring up the originating tab
missedGaps.why: Nothing activates a background tab when its page requests focus or its web notification is clicked. No 'focus' or notification handling in tabs.js wire() (tabs.js:140-240), and tabs are hidden WebContentsViews (setVisible false), so Meet/Calendar/Slack notification clicks may not switch tabs. Verify, then handle by activating tab.owner and focusing its window.

missedGaps.feature: Crashed-tab ('sad tab') and pinned-tab attention indicators in the strip
missedGaps.why: tab.crashed is never set to true: render-process-gone (tabs.js:179-185) only sets loading:false, and did-start-loading resets crashed (tabs.js:146). shell.js updateTabEl (:71-91) has no crashed or attention styling. Chrome shows a sad-tab favicon, and a dot on pinned tabs whose title changes in the background (Gmail, Slack).

missedGaps.feature: Importer: choose which Chrome/Edge profile to import from
missedGaps.why: profileDir() (importer/chromium.js:31-38) takes the first of 'Default' or 'Profile 1', so people with several Chrome profiles can't pick the one they use. Small add-on to the importer gap.

missedGaps.feature: Small Chrome shortcuts/mouse gestures not in the shortcuts gap: Shift+F5 hard reload (Windows), Alt+click a link to download it, F1 Help, Cmd+Shift+F toolbar in full screen (Mac), middle-click reload/new-tab button to open in a new tab
missedGaps.why: None appear in menu.js (:34-128) or shell.js. Each is a few lines and fits in the shortcuts batch.

missedGaps.feature: AppleScript / automation dictionary on macOS (niche)
missedGaps.why: Raycast, Alfred, Hookmark, Shortcuts and many productivity tools read the active tab URL and title from Chrome via AppleScript. Lumio has no scripting dictionary (sdef), only NSAppleEventsUsageDescription for its own outgoing use (build/package.mjs:83). Niche, but common among Mac power users.

missedGaps.feature: Insecure form submission warning (HTTPS page posting to HTTP) (niche)
missedGaps.why: Chrome's InsecureFormNavigationThrottle interstitial is in the Chrome layer, so Electron lacks it. Detect it in will-navigate/will-redirect: a POST from https to http in the main frame shows lumio://error?code=insecure-form with Send anyway / Go back.

wrongClaims.claim: Accessibility gap: 'Tabs have role=tab but #tabs has no tablist role… Add role=tablist, aria-selected'
wrongClaims.evidence: Already present. renderer/ui/shell.html:13 has <div id="tabs" role="tablist">, shell.js:59 sets role=tab and shell.js:75 sets aria-selected. Still missing: roving tabindex, arrow/Home/End keys, F6 cycling, listbox/option roles in the overlay, and focus rings.

wrongClaims.claim: Geolocation gap: 'macOS needs NSLocationUsageDescription in the Info.plist in build/package.mjs'
wrongClaims.evidence: Already set. build/package.mjs:86 has NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription (camera and mic at :84-85). Only the Windows location-provider part of this gap remains.

wrongClaims.claim: Importer gap: 'Decrypt Windows Chromium passwords with Local State os_crypt.encrypted_key via DPAPI … plus AES-GCM' (implied feasible for Chrome)
wrongClaims.evidence: Since Chrome 127, Windows Chrome uses App-Bound Encryption: 'v20' blobs whose key is wrapped by an elevated Chrome service, so user-level DPAPI decryption fails. This would work only for browsers still on v10 DPAPI (some Edge/Brave/Vivaldi builds). importer/chromium.js:8 already notes 'On Windows, Chrome locks passwords to itself'. Feasibility for Chrome should be 'no, use CSV'.

wrongClaims.claim: Per-site zoom gap: 'zoom() (tabs.js:415-421) sets the level but nothing persists it'
wrongClaims.evidence: Likely incorrect; needs a quick manual check. Electron documents setZoomLevel as using Chromium's same-origin zoom policy (HostZoomMap per host), so the level already applies to every tab of that host in the session. Electron's ZoomLevelDelegate also saves per-host levels in a persistent partition's Preferences ('persist:lumio', main.js:1269). The confirmed bugs are in the UI: shell.js:695 hides the badge on every tab switch, state() (tabs.js:493-516) carries no zoom value, and zoom from Ctrl+wheel or another tab of the same host never reaches the badge. Verify before adding a parallel zoomLevels store.

wrongClaims.claim: Certificate interstitial gap: 'bad-cert sites just show the generic error page (error.js:5-23)'
wrongClaims.evidence: The page isn't fully generic. error.js:13-15 already gives -200/-201/-202 certificate-specific titles, reached through did-fail-load (tabs.js:174-178). Still missing: the Advanced/Proceed path, certificate details and the omnibox 'Not secure' state.

wrongClaims.claim: alreadyHave: 'Tab status: … crashed page …' (implying a crashed state on the tab)
wrongClaims.evidence: The crashed flag is never set. render-process-gone (tabs.js:179-185) only does update({loading:false}) and loads lumio://error, and did-start-loading resets crashed:false (tabs.js:146). shell.js has no crashed styling, so the strip shows no crash. Only the error page exists.

wrongClaims.claim: alreadyHave: 'Downloads: … pause/resume/cancel/retry … toolbar progress ring and bubble'
wrongClaims.evidence: Pause, resume and retry are only on lumio://downloads (downloads.js:27-40). The toolbar bubble (overlay.js:24-43) offers only Cancel for running items and Open/Show for finished ones, with no retry for failed ones. The gap list's 'pause in bubble' is correct, but this alreadyHave line overstates the bubble.

wrongClaims.claim: Vertical tabs gap: 'Render the same tab state into the left sidebar (renderer/ui/sidebar.js already exists)'
wrongClaims.evidence: sidebar.js:1-4 is the Lumio AI sidebar (New task, Workflows, Templates, Scheduled, projects, chats), toggled by Cmd+Shift+S (menu.js:83). Vertical tabs would have to share or replace that column, so they need their own layout work. Not a cheap reuse.

There are three quit entries, at menu.js:29 (Mac app menu), menu.js:48 (Windows File > Exit) and menu.js:168 (the ⋮ menu). All three must route through the new hold-to-quit / downloads-in-progress logic.

The gap itself is real. Electron's default autoplayPolicy webPreference is 'no-user-gesture-required', and ensureView (tabs.js:76-85) doesn't set one. A cleaner fix is webPreferences.autoplayPolicy: 'document-user-activation-required' in ensureView, which is per tab view and doesn't affect the shell's own voice audio (renderer/ui/voice.js). A global switch would also cover the shell.

suggestedBatches.name: 1. Launch blockers and page-safety basics
features: DRM / Widevine playback (castlabs ECS + EVS VMP signing in build/package.mjs)
'Leave site?' beforeunload dialog (wc.close({waitForBeforeUnload}) at tabs.js:284 + will-prevent-unload)
Certificate error interstitial ('Your connection is not private' + Proceed)
HTTP Basic/Digest and proxy authentication dialog (app 'login')
External protocol links (openExternal permission + 'Open <app>?')
Pop-up blocker with omnibox 'blocked' icon and per-site allow
Popup windows get browser chrome (location bar, context menu, permissions, passwords) [missed]
Page unresponsive dialog (Wait / Exit page)
JavaScript dialogs: window.prompt + tab-modal alert/confirm
Fullscreen / pointer-lock exit notice [missed]
'Save … As…' always shows a Save dialog [missed]
Autoplay policy (webPreferences.autoplayPolicy)
Window-management permission becomes askable [missed]
macOS open-file for HTML/PDF [missed]
System settings: Windows background lifecycle (quit on window-all-closed unless background mode + Tray)
Crash reporting (opt-in)
Legal and credits pages (Terms, Privacy Policy, lumio://credits) [missed]
suggestedBatches.why: These are correctness, security and licensing issues every user can hit on day one (silent data loss on close, dead mailto/Zoom links, no way past a bad certificate, spam popups, hanging popup permissions, Netflix failing). They are mostly main-process handlers with small new overlay kinds, testable in e2e with local fixtures (beforeunload page, self-signed HTTPS server, 401 endpoint, window.open spam page). Swapping to castlabs Electron changes the runtime every later batch is tested on, so it goes first. New IPC channels must be whitelisted in preload/shell.js (INVOKE/SEND/EVENTS) and preload/dist rebuilt via scripts/build-preload.mjs. Any new overlay kinds should use CSS tokens from the start, because Batch 2 themes everything.

suggestedBatches.name: 2. Light / Device theme foundation (white mode)
features: White / light mode + 'Device' (follow system) theme mode
Tokenize shell.css, overlay.css, aura.css, pages.css and every page CSS; remove hard-coded colors in newtab.js MARK svg, settings.js, welcome.js, panel UI
Main-process colors follow the theme (window.js:59-60 titleBarOverlay/backgroundColor, tabs.js:88/165 internal-page bg, main.js:484 subscribe window, overlay/indicator views)
Accent palette with light-safe variants (THEME_COLORS icons.js:73) and accent propagated to all lumio:// pages (today only shell + settings.js:108 apply it)
Extension toolbar <browser-action-list> and popups readable in light mode
Incognito stays dark
Contrast check in tests/shell.test.mjs
suggestedBatches.why: White mode is an explicit user requirement, and it is a cross-cutting refactor of ~300 hard-coded colors that every later batch's new UI (bubbles, tab groups, ⋮ menu, side panel, settings pages) would otherwise multiply. Doing it second means later surfaces are built themeable once instead of re-themed. Set nativeTheme.themeSource so menus, prefers-color-scheme and the PDF viewer follow. Use a :root[data-theme] selector, and watch the existing data-theme attribute on the profile swatches (settings.js:107). Test by snapshotting the shell and each lumio:// page in light, dark and incognito (global.lumio.snapshot, main.js:1424).

suggestedBatches.name: 3. Everyday navigation, tabs and sessions
features: Link hover status bubble (URL at bottom-left)
Back/forward history dropdown (right-click / long-press) + middle-click
Mouse back/forward buttons and two-finger swipe navigation
Missing / conflicting Chrome keyboard shortcuts (Esc/Cmd+. stop, Ctrl+J downloads fix, view source, console, Cmd+Shift+Delete, Shift+F5, Alt+click download…)
Home button + home page setting; startup 'Open a specific page or set of pages'
Session restore with per-tab back/forward history, crash 'Restore pages?' and reopen-closed with history
Duplicate tab with back/forward history
Per-site zoom bubble, default page zoom (verify native per-host persistence first)
Find bar per-tab state, Cmd+E 'use selection'
Tab strip overflow scrolling with fade masks
Tab search (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A) across windows + recently closed
Tab context menu completeness + real 'Mute site' (per origin) + 'Move tab to another window ›' + strip context menu [missed]
Drop links/files/text onto the tab strip
Tear-off tabs / drag tabs between windows
Multi-select tabs (Shift/Cmd-click)
Quit / close warnings (hold Cmd+Q, many tabs, downloads in progress [missed])
Dock menu, Windows Jump List; dock/taskbar download progress and badge
Open File… (Cmd/Ctrl+O), Save page as HTML only / MHTML, trackpad pinch-zoom
Crashed-tab indicator in strip [missed]
Default-browser infobar [missed]
suggestedBatches.why: These are the core and common browsing behaviors people notice in the first hour, and they mostly touch tabs.js, shell.js, menu.js and main.js. Tab-model changes (multi-select, tear-off, overflow) should land before tab groups (Batch 4) build on the same startTabDrag/renderTabs code. Each item has a clear e2e check through global.lumio (tabs, cmd, snapshot).

suggestedBatches.name: 4. Organize and find: omnibox, bookmarks, tab groups, reading list, side panel
features: Omnibox remote search suggestions
Inline autocomplete and frecency learning in the omnibox
Omnibox: Switch to tab, @tabs/@bookmarks/@history/@lumio scopes, Actions
Omnibox details: paste and go, Shift+Delete, Alt/Shift/Ctrl+Enter, calculator
Omnibox zero-suggest on focus + clipboard link [missed]
Custom search engines, site search keywords and OpenSearch auto-detection; search engine choice in first run
Bookmark folders (tree model, bar folder popovers, 'Other bookmarks', manager tree, keep folders on import/export)
Bookmark star edit bubble and 'Bookmark all tabs' (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D)
Tab groups (create, name, colors, collapse, drag in/out, move to window, saved groups)
Reading list
General side panel framework (reading list, bookmarks, history, reading mode)
New Tab Page shortcuts: add/edit/remove/hide with undo
Sync more data types (folders tree-aware merge, reading list, saved groups)
Import from Firefox; keep folders; choose Chrome profile [missed]
suggestedBatches.why: These are data-model features that share storage and sync work. The bookmark tree migration (store.js flat list :218-269, applySyncedBookmarks, importers, export) and tab groups (tab model + session + sync) are the riskiest schema changes, so they ship together with migration tests (tests/store.test.mjs, sync-engine.test.mjs) and one sync adapter pass. The omnibox work is pure functions in omnibox.js with existing unit tests (tests/omnibox.test.mjs). New internal pages (e.g. lumio://sidepanel) need PAGE_HOSTS (protocol.js:21), ALL_PAGES (main.js:690) and the chrome:// alias regex (omnibox.js:17).

suggestedBatches.name: 5. Privacy, security and site controls
features: Permission prompts: 'Allow this time', omnibox-anchored chip/bubble, default per-category behavior
Site settings pages: All sites, per-permission allow/block lists, per-site detail, storage use
Per-site content toggles (JavaScript, images, insecure content, automatic downloads)
Third-party cookie controls (block in incognito / everywhere, exceptions)
Delete browsing data: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Delete, 15-minute range, time-ranged cookies/storage, counts
Clear cookies and site data when all windows close
HTTPS-First mode, scheme fallback and intranet hosts
Secure DNS (DNS-over-HTTPS)
Safe Browsing equivalent (blocklist interstitial) + dangerous/insecure download warnings
Certificate viewer, client certificates and Manage certificates
Password Checkup: compromised (breached) passwords; Safety check page
Lookalike / IDN spoofing protection; insecure form submission warning [missed]
Device choosers (USB, HID, Serial, Bluetooth) and File System Access permission
Built-in ad & tracker blocking; Privacy extras (DNT/GPC, WebRTC IP policy, auto-revoke)
Capture indicators on tabs + 'Sharing this tab' bar; share a single tab with audio [missed]
PDF handling setting; Autoplay/Sound per-site (shares mutedSites)
suggestedBatches.why: All of these go through the same Permissions/session plumbing (features.js ASKABLE/ALWAYS :137-138, request handler :174-198, sitePermissions in settings) and the Settings > Privacy and Site settings UI, so building the permission chip and site-settings pages once lets every category plug in. These are trust features a public browser is judged on. Test with local fixture servers (HTTP-only host for HTTPS-First, a blocklisted host for the interstitial, a getUserMedia page for 'Allow this time').

suggestedBatches.name: 6. Motion system and UI polish (best-in-class animations)
features: Polished UI motion system (FLIP tab open/close, width-freeze on close, spring drag settle, overlay enter/exit with transform-origin, find bar/infobar/bookmarks bar transitions, toast, omnibox icon slots)
Chrome-style ⋮ main menu on all platforms as an animated, themeable HTML overlay (zoom row, edit row, More tools, Help)
Tab hover cards (title, domain, preview image, memory)
Bookmark folder popovers, tab group collapse and side panel switch animations
Accessibility of browser UI: roving tabindex/arrow keys in tablist, F6 pane cycling, focus-visible rings, aria-live, prefers-reduced-motion/contrast/transparency
Customize panel: NTP background, custom color themes, toolbar customization, full URLs, density; Font settings
Energy Saver hook that disables UI animations
Omnibox rows with site favicons and staggered reveal
suggestedBatches.why: Polish goes after the new surfaces from Batches 1-5 exist, so one motion system (shared --spring easing, transform/opacity only, reduced-motion everywhere) covers all of them instead of being retrofitted piecemeal. It is a separate batch because it mostly touches shell.css, shell.js, overlay.css and overlay.js plus window.js hideOverlay, which needs an exit animation before removeChildView (window.js:154-162). WebContentsViews can't be CSS-animated, so animate the shell around them. Verify with screen recordings at 120Hz, the reduced-motion emulation and a frame-time budget in the shell tests.

suggestedBatches.name: 7. Platform depth and long tail
features: Multiple profiles, profile picker/switcher and Guest mode (note the hard-coded partition="persist:lumio" at shell.html:41)
Print preview with Save as PDF
Task Manager (Shift+Esc); Memory Saver modes/exceptions; Performance alerts; Preload pages; Back/forward cache test
Settings: search box, Languages, Accessibility, System, Reset; spell check settings; Accept-Language + UI i18n (EN/ES)
Translate pages; Reading mode with read aloud; Live Caption (post-launch)
Picture-in-Picture entry points; Global media controls hub
Share menu + QR code; Screenshot tool; Send tab to devices; Install site as app; Web Share API [missed]
Extensions UX (pin icons, site access, details, shortcuts, incognito) and API shims; extension NTP override
Address / payment card autofill, form history; Passkeys security keys + sync
Help center and Report an issue; Labs/version pages; DevTools docking
macOS menu bar parity, Look Up/Speech in context menus, Handoff, AppleScript dictionary [missed]
Page context menu additions (copy link text, link to highlight, video loop/controls/PiP, QR, emoji, frame source)
Name window; Vertical tabs; Split view; Keyboard shortcut customization; Caret browsing/autoscroll; Force dark; Protocol handlers
suggestedBatches.why: These are large, mostly independent subsystems, many partial on Electron or post-launch candidates. They can be built in parallel once the core, theme and polish batches are stable. Profiles go first inside this batch because they change how Store, sessions, extensions and sync are created (main.js:73 'normal' singleton) and would otherwise force rework of the features above. Split view and vertical tabs come after tab groups and multi-select (Batch 4) because they reuse that tab model and the layout() code (tabs.js:461-482).
